Q152.W10.body: After G-4, every earlier scene re-reads — the jokes, the errands, the interview. A quest that retroactively rewrites its own first half is doing with structure what twists usually fake with surprise.
Q152.W10.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W10.title: THE WHOLE SCRIPT REPLAYS ITSELF

Q152.W2.body: Every errand, in hindsight, was training for the seat: the fetch quests were rehearsals of rulership (someone pays, you pick who). The second-playthrough re-read is designed, not incidental.
Q152.W2.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W2.title: THE RECRUITMENT IS ONBOARDING

Q152.W3.body: The realm's succession law makes the player's murder lawful and the lawfulness makes it heavier — complicity with the paperwork done. The court's blessing removes the alibi of transgression.
Q152.W3.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W3.title: ACCESSION IS ASSASSINATION, FORMALIZED

Q152.W4.body: Thadon dies of pleasure, Syl dies of vindicated paranoia — each rite is a portrait of its throne. Method as characterization: the how of the kill IS the duchy's lore.
Q152.W4.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W4.title: THE MURDER WEARS THE VICTIM'S NATURE

Q152.W5.body: The joke character speaks plainly exactly one time, and the register break carries the reveal better than any exposition. A voice's consistency is a resource you spend once.
Q152.W5.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W5.title: THE DESPAIR SCENE CHANGES REGISTER, ONCE

Q152.W6.body: Sheogorath vanishes mid-scene and Jyggalag stands in his place — the twist performed as staging, not stated. The corpus's cleanest show-don't-tell at plot scale.
Q152.W6.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W6.title: THE SUBSTITUTION REVEAL

Q152.W7.body: Jyggalag's defeat frees him; the finale's violence is, from the enemy's side, a rescue. The duel re-reads as the curse's last formality — and the player's victory is also the antagonist's.
Q152.W7.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W7.title: THE BOSS WANTED TO LOSE

Q152.W8.body: Haskill's unimpressed continuity is the institution's real memory: staff as the realm's spine. The quietest worldbuilding in the expansion and its most load-bearing.
Q152.W8.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W8.title: THE CHAMBERLAIN OUTLIVES THE GOD

Q152.W9.body: The arc ends in an office, not a payout — succession as prize, with the timer attached. The genre's boldest ending shape, even underfunded (F1): what you win is what he was.
Q152.W9.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.W9.title: THE REWARD IS THE JOB

Q152.X1.body: After coronation, ruling amounts to a throne-room chair, a couple of petitioner novelties, and the chamberlain's shrug. The genre's boldest reward — BECOMING the god — ships with almost no verbs; the title is a hat. Community consensus for two decades: the ending writes a check the systems never cash. LAW: never grant an office without granting its VERBS. If Bohemia's fold ever seats a player in an institution (settlement head, faction chair, the throne-analog), the seat must come with the working ledger: petitions with stakes, policies with teeth (#151's gate policy is the scale model), succession paperwork of its own. An office without verbs is a cosmetic — cut it or staff it.
Q152.X1.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.X1.title: THE OFFICE IS A TROPHY, NOT A JOB

Q152.X2.body: Mania or Dementia colors the regalia and a handful of scenes, then the endgame funnels identically. The expansion's one exclusive moral fork — WHO the player murders for advancement — barely differentiates the world after; players compare notes and find mostly palette. LAW: an exclusive rite must write exclusive CONSEQUENCE — the court passed over should act like it (grudges, defections, a rival claimant), and the fold should read which throne was taken and how, at the finale (#140/#143's machinery exists for exactly this). If both branches converge, converge the STORY, never the ACCOUNTABILITY.
Q152.X2.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.X2.title: THE ACCESSION FORK IS WEIGHTLESS DOWNSTREAM

Q152.X3.body: The curse ends because the player wins a duel: no cost, no trade, no residue — the realm's thousand-era tragedy resolves as a boss health bar. Even sympathetic critics note the finale's metaphysics outweigh its mechanics: the deepest lore event in the setting is mechanically a Tuesday. LAW: breaking a cycle must cost cycle-denominated currency. Bohemia's generational frame prices this natively: ending a standing curse-class system (an Edict, #145; a faction's cyclical purge; the Greymarch-analog if one exists) should spend something only generations can bank — a lineage's accumulated record, a fold-held debt, an office's own continuity. Cheap exits from expensive cycles teach the player the cycle was never real. [PENDING, Paolo's call: what Bohemia's cycles even are — the law stands ready either way.]
Q152.X3.studyTitle: THE GREYMARCH (INHERITING THE MAD GOD'S OFFICE) (The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion — The Shivering Isles)
Q152.X3.title: THE CYCLE'S BREAKING IS FREE

Q153.N1.body: Entry: stage 2. He wants the stranger out of his profaned shrine and is not interested in their confusion. > "Where am I? What happened?" [gate: none] -> the first clue, delivered as complaint: how the player got here and who they wronged on the way > "I don't remember any of this." [gate: none] -> played straight; his disbelief IS the joke, and the reconstruction's premise > (apologize for a night you can't recall) [gate: none] -> the humor's engine: sincerity about an act you have no access to WHAT THIS NODE COSTS: nothing but dignity; the quest's currency is the player's mortification, spent freely.
Q153.N1.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.N1.title: NODE N-1 — the priest, waking

Q153.N2.body: Entry: stage 3. The jilted party, holding a grievance the player authored blind. > "I agreed to marry you?" [gate: none] -> the farce and, under it, a real ache the quest declines to fully play for laughs > "Tell me what I did." [gate: none] -> another fragment of the night; the crime scene is testimony > (offer to make it right) [gate: none] -> partial restitution; the comedy has a conscience NOVERB "Let me just remember it myself" — no flashback is offered. The night is UNRECOVERABLE except through the people it touched. The removed verb is the whole design: a blackout is reconstructed socially or not at all.
Q153.N2.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.N2.title: NODE N-2 — a witness (the wedding thread)

Q153.N3.body: Entry: stage 4. Sam drops the disguise: the Prince of revelry, delighted. > "You did all this to me?" [gate: none] -> he doesn't deny it; the author enjoying the reconstruction he wrote > "Why?" [gate: none] -> because it was fun, and because you were worth the audition. THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK, paraphrased: the best nights are the ones you have to piece together afterward > (take the Rose) [gate: night reconstructed] -> the reward, an approval, a door to more mischief
Q153.N3.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.N3.title: NODE N-3 — Sanguine revealed

Q153.P1.body: system: the release-valve quest layer / the unrecorded ledger / dialogue scenes A Bohemia quest where the dynast loses a night (drink, a fever, a fold-skip, an Amalgamation edit) and must RECONSTRUCT it by interviewing the people it touched — comedy on the surface, a memory-gap detective story underneath, deeply on-theme for a game about the edited record. ``` @TALK blackout_witness speaker=neighbor entry=night_lost @SAY You don't remember. Of course you don't. You were three
Q153.P1.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.P1.title: PORT 1 — THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION QUEST [W1, W4, W5 — the core port]

Q153.P2.body: system: the missing-persons organ (#141) / the fold The reconstruction can conclude FALSE — the dynast pieces together a version of their lost night that didn't happen, accuses their own blackout self of the wrong grievance, and the fold records both the believed version and the true one. Any later system may surface the gap. A blackout you can only reassemble correctly is a corridor; ours can be honestly misremembered.
Q153.P2.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.P2.title: PORT 2 — THE RECONSTRUCTION THAT ASSEMBLES WRONG [F1's law]

Q153.P3.body: system: faction memory / the conduct book (#143) Most of a blackout's harm is comic and resets; ONE grievance persists — a person who stays hurt, a debt the district remembers, a reputation dinged. The release valve earns its lightness by letting exactly one thing not be funny, and the fold carries it.
Q153.P3.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.P3.title: PORT 3 — ONE GRIEVANCE STICKS [F2's law]

Q153.P4.body: system: the fold / the dial / conscience When a Bohemia quest offers a VOLUNTARY loss of control (drink to oblivion, elect a memory edit, skip a fold beat), the choosing is itself a recorded act with a cost: the dynast elected absence, and something happened while they were gone that they now own. The voluntary blackout as a moral act, not just a setup.
Q153.P4.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.P4.title: PORT 4 — CHOOSING TO NOT BE PRESENT [F3's law]

Q153.W1.body: The mystery is your own off-screen night, so the detective work is self-confrontation — the rarest and best investigation subject: yourself, unwatched.
Q153.W1.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W1.title: THE PLAYER IS THE CRIMINAL

Q153.W10.body: Placed among Skyrim's grim Daedric quests, the levity relieves and, by contrast, sharpens the dread of the darker ones. Range is the point.
Q153.W10.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W10.title: THE TONE IS A COUNTERWEIGHT

Q153.W2.body: Inverted dramatic irony: every NPC is a witness to a you that you can't access, and their straight-faced grievances are the comedy engine.
Q153.W2.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W2.title: THE WORLD KNOWS WHAT YOU DON'T

Q153.W3.body: The quest never winks; the priest and the bride treat the aftermath as real, and the player's mortified reconstruction lands because nobody in it is laughing.
Q153.W3.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W3.title: SINCERITY IS THE JOKE

Q153.W4.body: The night is reassembled from people, not flashback — a social reconstruction that makes the witnesses the level design.
Q153.W4.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W4.title: THE CRIME SCENE IS TESTIMONY

Q153.W5.body: No flashback verb exists; the player must go ask, which turns a memory gap into a tour of the people it touched.
Q153.W5.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W5.title: THE BLACKOUT IS UNRECOVERABLE DIRECTLY

Q153.W6.body: The jilted wedding keeps the comedy from weightlessness — one witness whose grievance has an ache, played almost straight.
Q153.W6.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W6.title: THE HUMAN NOTE UNDER THE FARCE

Q153.W7.body: Sanguine was auditioning the player through chaos; the reconstruction was the résumé — the reward reframes the whole night as a test passed.
Q153.W7.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W7.title: THE BENDER IS A JOB INTERVIEW

Q153.W8.body: Contest to Rose in one arc; the comedy never dilutes because the container is tight — the release valve does one thing perfectly.
Q153.W8.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W8.title: SCOPE DISCIPLINE

Q153.W9.body: At each witness the player may make amends or not, with no mechanical push — the conscience slot is real and entirely theirs.
Q153.W9.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.W9.title: RESTITUTION IS OPTIONAL AND UNJUDGED

Q153.X1.body: The witnesses come in a fixed order and the player cannot investigate wrong, reach a false conclusion, or miss a beat — the "detective" work is a guided tour of pre-written comedy. The mystery cannot fail, so it is a delivery mechanism, not a deduction. LAW: a reconstruction quest must be ABLE to assemble wrong — the player accuses their own blackout self of something they didn't do, or misses a witness and carries a false version — with the world recording the gap. A blackout you can only reassemble one correct way is a cutscene with steps.
Q153.X1.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.X1.title: THE RECONSTRUCTION IS A CORRIDOR

Q153.X2.body: The jilted bride, the sold goat, the trashed tavern — none of it persists; the world resets, no witness stays wronged, the wedding thread's ache evaporates on quest completion. The comedy is consequence-free, which is safe and also thin. LAW: at least one grievance from a blackout must STICK — a person who stays hurt, a debt that stays owed, a reputation the district remembers. Release-valve comedy earns its lightness by letting one thing not be funny.
Q153.X2.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.X2.title: THE HARM HAS NO WEIGHT

Q153.X3.body: The player CHOOSES to drink into oblivion and the quest never asks why or costs them the choosing — the loss of control is pure setup, never a theme. For a game about edited memory, that is a missed depth. LAW: if a Bohemia quest offers a voluntary blackout (drink, a memory edit, a fold-skip), the CHOICE to lose control should itself be a recorded act with a cost — the player elected not to be present, and something happened in their absence they now own.
Q153.X3.studyTitle: A NIGHT TO REMEMBER (THE BLACKOUT RECONSTRUCTION) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q153.X3.title: THE VOLUNTARY BLACKOUT ISN'T INTERROGATED

Q154.N1.body: Entry: stage 2. Not a person — a message, left where the player will find it after the first clue. > (read: "STOP investigating, or else") [gate: none] -> the city speaking; the quest's turn from mystery to threat > (keep pulling the thread anyway) [gate: none] -> escalation; the investigation becomes the offense NOVERB "Take this to an honest authority" — no honest authority exists in Markarth. The removed verb is the quest's thesis: there is no clean institution to appeal to, because the institution is the crime.
Q154.N1.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.N1.title: NODE M-1 — the warning note

Q154.N2.body: Entry: stage 4. The King in Rags, running a war from a cell, sizing up the framed newcomer. > "You're behind the murders." [gate: none] -> he doesn't deny it; his cause and his killings are one thing, stated without apology > "Get me out of here." [gate: none] -> his terms: help his people escape, in blood. THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK, paraphrased: the city calls it order; we call it what was taken > "Why are you still alive down here?" [gate: none] -> the Silver-Bloods keep him, using his war to justify their grip — the frame's real architecture > (say nothing; weigh the pit) [gate: none] SILENCE -> the mine's full misery on the record before the choice
Q154.N2.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.N2.title: NODE M-2 — Madanach in the mine

Q154.N3.body: Entry: stage 5. The escape, and whose bodies it runs over. > "We go together." (side with Madanach) [gate: none] -> the uprising; guards die, the Forsworn walk out, a unique armor, the player free and complicit in a massacre > "I'll take the other deal." (betray him) [gate: none] -> the corrupt order's cleaner exit; Madanach's people die, the player free and complicit in the suppression > NOVERB "I'll expose the Silver-Bloods" — no line exists. The real criminals are beyond the fork; the player may only choose which victim-oppressor walks. The removed verb is the quest's cruelty: you cannot punish the power, only pick its instrument.
Q154.N3.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.N3.title: NODE M-3 — the fork

Q154.P1.body: system: the district / faction web / the unrecorded ledger A Bohemia arc where pulling one thread on a quiet wrong turns the DISTRICT itself against the dynast — its enforcers, its powers, its prosperity all one machine defending a buried crime. Investigation reframed as the offense; the district's order revealed as a lie the powerful maintain. ``` @TALK the_warning speaker=fixer entry=thread_pulled @SAY You found a loose brick and started pulling. Stop.
Q154.P1.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.P1.title: PORT 1 — THE DISTRICT THAT FRAMES YOU [W1, W2, W3 — the core port]

Q154.P2.body: system: the fold / faction memory The arc's real power is beyond the dynast's reach NOW — but the fold plants a discoverable thread by which a later generation can make them answer, or at least a record that NAMES them. Untouchable-by-design carries its own future reckoning, so the cruelty is deliberate, not unfinished.
Q154.P2.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.P2.title: PORT 2 — THE UNTOUCHABLE WITH A LATER THREAD [F1's law]

Q154.P3.body: system: conscience / the unrecorded ledger If looking is punished, the dynast may CHOOSE to stop — and live free, ignorant, complicit-by-omission, in a district whose wound stays buried. The fold records the choice to not-know. Forced imprisonment removes the very agency the theme is about; ours keeps it, and prices the looking-away.
Q154.P3.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.P3.title: PORT 3 — THE RIGHT TO STOP LOOKING [F2's law]

Q154.P4.body: system: the faction web / Liberate-Respect-Become adjacency When the dynast must choose which victim-oppressor to free, both routes STAIN — an uprising's blood or a cover-up's complicity — and the district remembers which. The Pacifist Law still holds a third, harder path (expose the architect at ruinous cost), but the default fork refuses innocence. [PENDING, Paolo's call: the factions.]
Q154.P4.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.P4.title: PORT 4 — NO CLEAN EXIT, WHICHEVER OPPRESSED YOU SERVE [W6, W8]

Q154.W1.body: Not a villain in the city — the city itself: guards, jarl, market, mine, one machine that turns on the player for looking. The best "the institution is the crime" structure in the game.
Q154.W1.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W1.title: THE CITY IS THE ANTAGONIST

Q154.W10.body: Neither ending fixes Markarth; the player leaves a place still sick, still quiet about it. The refusal to resolve is the point — some rots outlast the visitor who found them.
Q154.W10.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W10.title: THE WOUND STAYS OPEN

Q154.W2.body: The player is framed and jailed FOR asking; curiosity is reframed as the crime, which is a chillingly real depiction of how closed systems defend themselves.
Q154.W2.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W2.title: INVESTIGATION IS THE OFFENSE

Q154.W3.body: Markarth's silver, order, and tidy market sit directly on the wound the quest uncovers — the peace and the crime are the same structure.
Q154.W3.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W3.title: THE PROSPERITY IS BUILT ON THE SUPPRESSION

Q154.W4.body: Every authority is compromised; the removed "honest authority" verb is the thesis. There is nowhere to take the truth.
Q154.W4.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W4.title: NO CLEAN INSTITUTION TO APPEAL TO

Q154.W5.body: The Silver-Bloods engineer it all and pay nothing; the fork lets you choose their instrument, never punish them — a bitter, adult depiction of where power actually sits.
Q154.W5.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W5.title: THE REAL POWER IS UNTOUCHABLE

Q154.W6.body: Both escape routes stain the player — an uprising's massacre or a cover-up's complicity. The quest refuses to let anyone leave innocent.
Q154.W6.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W6.title: NO CLEAN EXIT

Q154.W7.body: The full picture is only available inside the mine the city threw the player into — the geography of the cover-up is the quest's structure.
Q154.W7.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W7.title: THE TRUTH LIVES WHERE IT WAS BURIED

Q154.W8.body: Madanach is a freedom-fighter and a murderer, the same act; the Silver-Bloods are order and oppression, the same act. No side is clean, and the quest names it.
Q154.W8.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W8.title: THE SYMPATHETIC-AND-TERRIBLE FORK

Q154.W9.body: Note, then guards, then prison — the city's hostility rises in readable steps, so the trap closes at a pace the player feels shutting.
Q154.W9.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.W9.title: THE FRAME ESCALATES LEGIBLY

Q154.X1.body: The Silver-Bloods engineer everything and face no reckoning, which is thematically sharp — but the quest offers no path even to make them PAY later, no thread that resurfaces, so their untouchability reads as an unfinished quest rather than a deliberate cruelty. LAW: when a quest's real power is deliberately beyond reach, plant a DISCOVERABLE later thread — a way the untouchable can be made to answer generations on, or at least a record that names them. Untouchable-by-design must be distinguishable from untouchable-because-unfinished; the fold is how.
Q154.X1.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.X1.title: THE REAL VILLAIN CAN'T BE TOUCHED, AND THE GAME DOESN'T LET THAT LAND

Q154.X2.body: Once the investigation starts, the imprisonment is unavoidable; a cautious player who reads the warning and stops is railroaded into the mine anyway. The "investigating is the crime" theme is undercut by the player having no real agency to heed the warning. LAW: if looking is punished, let the player CHOOSE to stop looking, with a real (worse-in-other-ways) consequence — a district where the wound stays buried and the player stays free, ignorant, and complicit-by-omission. Forced imprisonment removes the choice the theme is about.
Q154.X2.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.X2.title: THE FRAME PUNISHES CURIOSITY WITH NO OFF-RAMP

Q154.X3.body: Madanach and his people exist mostly to be the escape's other lever; their cause gets one speech and their victimhood is told, not felt, so the "sympathetic terrorist" lands thinner than the setup earns. LAW: a faction the player is asked to free or betray needs enough prior PRESENCE that the choice has felt weight — witnessed grievances, named individuals, seen suppression — not a single cell-block monologue. Earn the fork with worldbuilding, not exposition.
Q154.X3.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY / NO ONE ESCAPES CIDHNA MINE (THE CITY THAT FRAMED YOU) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q154.X3.title: THE FORSWORN ARE FLATTENED TO THE FORK

Q155.N1.body: Entry: stage 2. The curse's leader, arguing for mercy with unsettling reason. > "You're the monsters killing the elves." [gate: none] -> her correction: the werewolves are cursed humans; the elves' keeper is the source > "Tell me how this started." [gate: none] -> the old atrocity, the vengeance, Zathrian's grief — the truth commission opens > "What do you want?" [gate: none] -> peace, and an end to being a monster. THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK, paraphrased: we did not choose this shape; the one who chose it for us still walks free among your allies > (say nothing; look at the werewolves as people) [gate: none] SILENCE -> the encounter reframes the hunt entirely; the beasts become the bereaved
Q155.N1.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.N1.title: NODE B-1 — the Lady of the Forest

Q155.N2.body: Entry: stage 4. The wound, cornered by its own truth. He defends the vengeance; the player must make him face that it has outlived its justice. > "Everyone who wronged you is dead. This has to end." [gate: PERSUASION / the truth assembled] -> the hard path: he FORGIVES, and the game's best ending opens > "The curse is you. Admit it." [gate: none] -> he cannot, at first; his identity is the wound; pushing is the quest's real boss fight, fought in words > "Then we do this your way." [gate: none] -> side with the elves; the werewolves die > NOVERB "Let's just cure the elves and leave the werewolves alone" — no line exists; the curse is one thing, the elves and werewolves bound to the same wound. The removed verb is the quest's cruelty: you cannot spare both without Zathrian's forgiveness, and forgiveness is the one thing he won't sell.
Q155.N2.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.N2.title: NODE B-2 — Zathrian confronted

Q155.N3.body: Entry: stage 5. The wound closes, or is fed again. > (Zathrian forgives, dies willingly) [gate: persuasion won] -> the curse lifts for ALL; elves and werewolves both live; the grief finally put down > (slaughter the werewolves) [gate: none] -> elves cured, victims murdered; the wound answered with more wound > (kill Zathrian, side with werewolves) [gate: none] -> the cursed freed, the elves he protected doomed; the vengeance turned around WHAT THIS NODE COSTS: the peace costs Zathrian his life and his grievance; the blood options cost a whole people; there is no exit where nobody pays.
Q155.N3.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.N3.title: NODE B-3 — the resolution

Q155.P1.body: system: the Amalgamation / the fold / faction web A Bohemia arc where a "monster" or an Amalgamation-plague turns out to be an old wound in another form — a grievance a prior generation refused to release, still killing people who never committed the original crime. The hunt becomes a truth commission; the resolution is about the WOUND. ``` @TALK the_curse_speaks speaker=lady entry=forest_inverted @SAY You came to kill us. Look closer. We were pe
Q155.P1.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.P1.title: PORT 1 — THE CURSE THAT IS A GRIEVANCE [W1, W2, W5 — the core port]

Q155.P2.body: system: [READ] / the fold / Liberate adjacency The best ending — releasing the wound — is gated on the dynast having RECONSTRUCTED the grievance's full history (the crime, the vengeance, the long feeding), not on a persuasion number. A player who does the moral work can always reach the peace; the check tests knowing. This is Liberate's mechanic: you can only make someone let go if you understand what they're holding.
Q155.P2.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.P2.title: PORT 2 — FORGIVENESS GATED ON UNDERSTANDING, NOT A STAT [F1's law]

Q155.P3.body: system: the fold / the ~100-year arc The grievance the dynast is asked to help release was WITNESSED — a prior generation's atrocity and its refusal to forgive, seen in play, so a later dynast's forgiveness carries the weight of a history they lived. The fold does what Nature of the Beast could only exposit: it lets the player see the centuries.
Q155.P3.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.P3.title: PORT 3 — THE WOUND SHOWN ACROSS GENERATIONS [F2's law]

Q155.P4.body: system: entities / faction web An Amalgamation-plague or cursed faction that the arc humanizes keeps NAMED individuals present through the resolution, so that choosing to wipe them out costs the weight the reveal promised. Humanize through the ending, not just the twist — the fold remembers each face erased.
Q155.P4.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.P4.title: PORT 4 — THE HUMANIZED FACTION KEEPS ITS FACES [F3's law]

Q155.W1.body: The quest opens as a straight beast-kill and becomes the excavation of an old mutual atrocity — the genre's cleanest bait-and-switch from violence to history.
Q155.W1.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W1.title: THE MONSTER HUNT IS A TRUTH COMMISSION

Q155.W10.body: Zathrian can only release the wound by dying with it — the peace is not free, it is paid by the one who held the grief. Letting go is the last thing he does.
Q155.W10.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W10.title: THE FORGIVENESS IS A DEATH

Q155.W2.body: The werewolves are a wound wearing fur; the plague is grief that wouldn't die. The monster is literally somebody's refusal to forgive.
Q155.W2.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W2.title: THE CURSE IS A GRIEVANCE IN ANIMAL FORM

Q155.W3.body: Humans wronged elves, elves cursed humans, the cursed kill the innocent — no one is clean, and the quest names the whole chain.
Q155.W3.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W3.title: EVERY PARTY IS VICTIM AND PERPETRATOR

Q155.W4.body: Zathrian is the victim who became the perpetrator by refusing to heal — the hardest, truest kind of antagonist, sympathetic and culpable at once.
Q155.W4.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W4.title: THE VILLAIN IS THE WRONGED PARTY

Q155.W5.body: The three endings are three answers to "feed the grievance or release it" — the monsters are the symptom, the grief is the disease.
Q155.W5.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W5.title: THE RESOLUTION IS ABOUT THE WOUND, NOT THE MONSTERS

Q155.W6.body: Peace requires convincing the wronged to stop being wronged — the hardest human act, gated as the game's hardest outcome. Mercy is earned, not given.
Q155.W6.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W6.title: THE BEST ENDING IS FORGIVENESS

Q155.W7.body: Peace costs Zathrian his life; blood costs a whole people. The quest refuses an exit where nobody pays, which is what makes the choice real.
Q155.W7.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W7.title: NO COST-FREE PATH

Q155.W8.body: The Lady of the Forest makes the case for mercy with unsettling calm — the "beast" is the most morally lucid voice in the forest.
Q155.W8.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W8.title: THE MONSTERS ARGUE REASONABLY

Q155.W9.body: No living person committed the original wrong, yet it still demands blood — the clearest depiction of how inherited grievance outlives its cause.
Q155.W9.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.W9.title: THE CRIME IS CENTURIES DEAD AND STILL KILLING

Q155.X1.body: Peace is gated behind a persuasion stat; a player who understands the situation perfectly but lacks the check is forced into blood. The forgiveness that is the quest's moral heart is bought with a dialogue skill, not with the player's comprehension. LAW: the hardest, best outcome must be gated on ASSEMBLED UNDERSTANDING (evidence, the truth reconstructed, the wound's history known), not a raw stat — so that a player who does the moral work can always reach it, and the check tests knowing, not build. (#38/#17's lesson: earn the argument with the case.)
Q155.X1.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.X1.title: THE BEST ENDING IS A SKILL-CHECK, NOT AN EARNED TRUTH

Q155.X2.body: The keeper's grief is exposited in a few lines; the player never witnessed the atrocity, the vengeance, or the long feeding of the wound, so his refusal to forgive reads as stubbornness rather than a tragedy the player understands from inside. LAW: a wound the player is asked to help release must be SHOWN across the arc — the original crime witnessed, the grief's long persistence seen (the fold is built for this: a grievance the player watched a prior generation refuse to put down). Told grief cannot carry a forgiveness this heavy.
Q155.X2.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.X2.title: ZATHRIAN'S CENTURIES ARE TOLD, NOT FELT

Q155.X3.body: After the humanizing reveal, the werewolves become mostly the "other lever" in the ending; their individual personhood (glimpsed in the reveal) doesn't carry into the resolution, so slaughtering them costs less than the setup earned. LAW: a humanized "monster" faction must keep its individual faces through the RESOLUTION — named victims present at the choice, so that wiping them out has the weight the reveal promised. Humanize through the ending, not just the twist.
Q155.X3.studyTitle: NATURE OF THE BEAST (THE CURSE IS A WOUND, NOT A MONSTER) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q155.X3.title: THE WEREWOLVES REVERT TO STAKES AT THE FORK

Q156.N1.body: Entry: stage 3. The maker, indicting his own masterpiece. He explains what the golems are and begs for the Anvil's destruction. > "The golems are people?" [gate: none] -> the atrocity confirmed: conscious dwarves bound living into metal, forever > "It could save the dwarves, though." [gate: none] -> he doesn't deny the power; he denies that the power is worth the price. THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK, paraphrased: I made it, I know what it can do, and I have spent three hundred years learning what it costs > "Why should I destroy the one thing that could win the war?" [gate: none] -> because a victory built of slaves is the thing you were fighting against > (say nothing; look at the golems) [gate: none] SILENCE -> their conscious misery on the record before the choice
Q156.N1.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.N1.title: NODE A-1 — Caridin

Q156.N2.body: Entry: stage 4. The ends, unrepentant. She wants the Anvil and will not pretend the cost troubles her. > "You killed your whole House for this." [gate: none] -> she does not flinch; the dwarves are dying and this saves them, and she has already paid what it took > "Hespith. Your wife." [gate: none] -> the price made personal; she has spent even that > "The Anvil is slavery." [gate: none] -> and slavery, she argues, is cheaper than extinction — the ends' whole case, stated cleanly > NOVERB "Let's take the Anvil but never use it that way" — no line exists; the Anvil is what it is, and having it is being willing to use it. The removed verb is the fork's honesty: you cannot own the atrocity-tool and keep clean hands about it.
Q156.N2.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.N2.title: NODE A-2 — Branka

Q156.N3.body: Entry: stage 4-5. The forge kept or broken; a Paragon dead either way. > (side with Caridin, destroy the Anvil) [gate: none] -> the tool that could save everyone is thrown away to end the atrocity; Branka dies; Caridin forges the crown, then chooses his own end > (side with Branka, keep the Anvil) [gate: none] -> the weapon is claimed; Caridin dies; the dwarves gain an army of slaves and the player owns that choice > (a middle, if maneuvered) [gate: careful play] -> Branka's obsession still ends her; the Anvil's fate still forks; the game resists a clean "everyone lives" WHAT THIS NODE COSTS: a Paragon's life whichever way, and either the tool or the soul — the descent's whole point was to force this trade.
Q156.N3.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.N3.title: NODE A-3 — the fork

Q156.P1.body: system: the Amalgamation / the fold / the endgame The Amalgamation IS an Anvil: a technology that promises to save everyone by consuming people, defended by a true believer whose case is genuinely strong. A Bohemia arc where the dynast finds the tool that could end the crisis and learns every unit of it is a murdered volunteer — the means-vs-ends machine at civilizational scale. ``` @TALK the_maker_regrets speaker=caridin entry=anvil_revealed @SA
Q156.P1.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.P1.title: PORT 1 — THE ANVIL AS THE AMALGAMATION [W1, W4, W7 — the core port]

Q156.P2.body: system: the endgame / the difficulty of Liberate The "use the tool" path (Become) must be genuinely tempting — the salvation real, present, costed, not pre-buried under obvious monstrosity. If destroying the Amalgamation is obviously correct, it is a difficulty setting; the Liberate ending only means something if Become was a real temptation with a real case. (Q126's honest-devil law, at endgame scale.)
Q156.P2.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.P2.title: PORT 2 — MAKE THE ENDS TEMPTING [F1's law]

Q156.P3.body: system: the Amalgamation / [READ] / SOMA-adjacency (#34) The price of the Amalgamation-Anvil has its OWN voices — the uploaded dead speak directly for what was done to them, not only through the maker and the believer. The dynast hears the consumed, so the atrocity is heard, not just described. SOMA's abandoned self is the model: the price screaming in the chair behind you.
Q156.P3.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.P3.title: PORT 3 — THE CONSUMED TESTIFY [F2's law]

Q156.P4.body: system: the fold / [READ] / Liberate If a less-costly resolution exists, its path is discoverable IN-WORLD — a reachable insight, a reconstructed truth — never walkthrough-only, so the dynast who does the moral work can find the mercy. The #26/#155 earned-outcome law applied to the endgame's hardest fork.
Q156.P4.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.P4.title: PORT 4 — THE GENTLER PATH IS DISCOVERABLE [F3's law]

Q156.W1.body: The golem-army isn't guarded by an atrocity — it IS one; every unit a murdered soul. The weapon and the crime are the same object, which is the purest means-vs-ends form.
Q156.W1.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W1.title: THE TOOL IS MADE OF THE ATROCITY

Q156.W10.body: Players argue the Anvil choice for years — the sign the dilemma was real. A tool worth its atrocity has no settled answer, and the quest is honest enough not to give one.
Q156.W10.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W10.title: THE QUESTION SURVIVES THE CREDITS

Q156.W2.body: The descent walks the player through Branka's dead House and Hespith's ruin before revealing the Anvil — you feel the price before you see what it buys.
Q156.W2.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W2.title: THE COST IS SHOWN BEFORE THE PRIZE

Q156.W3.body: Caridin built the Anvil and wants it destroyed, having lived inside its cost for centuries — the most credible possible witness against a tool: its inventor.
Q156.W3.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W3.title: THE MAKER TURNS AGAINST HIS MASTERPIECE

Q156.W4.body: Branka is not lying — the dwarves are dying and the Anvil could save them. The dilemma is real because the monstrous option might actually work.
Q156.W4.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W4.title: THE ENDS HAVE A REAL CASE

Q156.W5.body: Keep the tool and own the slavery; destroy it and forgo the salvation. Both cost a Paragon and a principle; the game refuses a free exit.
Q156.W5.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W5.title: NO CLEAN FORK

Q156.W6.body: Branka spent her own wife; the atrocity has a face the antagonist loved. The abstraction of "souls bound to metal" gets a name.
Q156.W6.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W6.title: THE PRICE IS PERSONAL

Q156.W7.body: Branka is a good goal pursued past every line, not evil for its own sake — the scariest antagonist is the one whose ends you can't dismiss.
Q156.W7.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W7.title: THE VILLAIN ISN'T ONE

Q156.W8.body: The whole descent is for a succession crown; the means-vs-ends fork is nested inside a governance need, so the choice has downstream weight beyond itself.
Q156.W8.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W8.title: THE POLITICAL STAKES FRAME THE MORAL ONES

Q156.W9.body: Caridin, if he wins, unmakes his creation and then himself — the atrocity's author choosing to end with it. Letting go is a death he chooses.
Q156.W9.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.W9.title: THE MAKER PAYS LAST

Q156.X1.body: The dwarves ARE dying; the Anvil COULD save them; Branka's utilitarian case is genuinely strong — but the quest stacks the presentation so heavily toward "she's a monster" (the dead House, mad Hespith) that the ends-side is emotionally foreclosed before the argument is fair. The hardest version would make keeping the Anvil genuinely tempting. LAW: when a quest forks on means-vs-ends, the ENDS must be made genuinely tempting — the salvation real, present, and costed, not pre-buried under the villain's atrocities. If the "use the tool" path is obviously monstrous, it is a difficulty setting, not a dilemma (Q126's F1 law, at civilizational scale).
Q156.X1.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.X1.title: BRANKA IS RIGHT AND THE GAME UNDERSELLS IT

Q156.X2.body: The murdered-volunteer horror is delivered mostly through Caridin and Hespith; the individual golems, the actual price, are largely mute scenery. The atrocity is told about more than it is heard from. LAW: the PRICE of an atrocity-tool must have its own voices — the consumed should testify directly, not only through the maker and the madwoman. Let the Amalgamation's uploaded speak for what was done to them (SOMA's abandoned Simon, #34, is the model).
Q156.X2.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.X2.title: THE GOLEMS DON'T GET TO SPEAK FOR THEMSELVES ENOUGH

Q156.X3.body: A player can maneuver a less-bloody resolution, but only via non-obvious dialogue paths; the clean-ish outcome is gated behind meta-knowledge rather than the player's understanding, so most players hit a harder ending without knowing a gentler one existed. LAW: if a gentler resolution exists, its PATH must be discoverable in-world (a clue, a reachable insight), not walkthrough-only — so that the player who does the moral work can find the mercy, per the #26/#155 earned-outcome law.
Q156.X3.studyTitle: A PARAGON OF HER KIND / THE ANVIL OF THE VOID (THE ENDS THAT EAT THE MEANS) (Dragon Age: Origins)
Q156.X3.title: THE "EVERYONE LIVES" MIDDLE IS A HIDDEN SKILL PUZZLE

[gate: none] -> the grief under the armor; the law does not bend, and that is its horror > "Is there no cure?" [gate: none] -> none; the nature is what it is; Morinth is a person and a killer both > "Why the code?" [gate: none] -> because without it she could not do what must be done. THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK, paraphrased: the law is the only thing that lets me survive being her mother
Q157.N1.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.N1.title: NODE Y-1 — Samara on the law

Q157.N2.body: Entry: stage 4. The monster making her case. Alone with the bait, she charms, escalates, and offers a way out of her mother's law. > "Your mother is hunting you." [gate: none] -> her framing: the law is the prison, she is its victim; a case that lands because it is partly true > "Tell me what you are." [gate: none] -> the Ardat-Yakshi nature, delivered as tragedy, not confession — the seduction's core: not my fault > "What are you offering?" [gate: none] -> power, freedom, a life without the law. THE HOOK, paraphrased: help me end her, and I will show you what you could never survive with anyone else > (resist / hold composure) [gate: WILL / the player's judgment] -> the trap holds; Samara arrives; the fork opens honestly > (yield to her) [gate: none] TRAP -> the player is being drawn into siding with the killer; the seduction working on the one who was meant to be baiting it NOVERB "Let's find a way to save you without killing anyone" — no line exists; the Ardat-Yakshi nature admits no cure, and the fork admits no both-live. The removed verb is the tragedy: one of these women dies,
Q157.N2.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.N2.title: NODE Y-2 — Morinth's seduction

Q157.N3.body: Entry: stage 5. Mother and daughter, grappling, the player's hand the deciding weight. > "Samara, now." (help the mother) [gate: none] -> Morinth dies; the law is fulfilled; the justicar survives, grieving, loyal > "Do it, Morinth." (help the daughter) [gate: seduced or chosen] -> Samara dies; Morinth replaces her, posing as her mother; the player has sided with a serial killer and armed her > WHAT THIS NODE COSTS: one of them, always. Back the law and a person born into a killing body dies; back the person and a murderer walks free wearing her mother's face.
Q157.N3.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.N3.title: NODE Y-3 — the fork

Q157.P1.body: system: the Amalgamation / dialogue scenes / [READ] A Bohemia arc where the dynast must draw out a threat by posing as its prey, and the threat SEDUCES — makes a real case, offers real power, and can talk the player into the wrong choice in the moment. The Amalgamation's seduction (#34/#36) made intimate: the archive that promises to save the dead, arguing directly to the one sent to end it. ``` @TALK the_seduction speaker=morinth entry=alone_with_
Q157.P1.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.P1.title: PORT 1 — THE SEDUCTION THAT TESTS THE PLAYER [W2, W3, W4 — the core port]

Q157.P2.body: system: the fork / Become adjacency The seductive-but-dangerous choice must carry a REAL upside the dynast forgoes by refusing — power, knowledge, a genuine good — so resisting costs something and the temptation is honest, not a trap with a penalty. This is the Become ending's mechanic: siding with the Amalgamation must be genuinely tempting, or Liberate means nothing (#156's F1 law, restated intimate).
Q157.P2.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.P2.title: PORT 2 — THE SEDUCTIVE CHOICE WITH A REAL UPSIDE [F1's law]

Q157.P3.body: system: the fold / conscience When the dynast kills a humanized threat born into its nature, the arc leaves ROOM to mourn what was unavoidable — an aftermath beat, a fold entry that carries the loss as grief, not a closed case. The Amalgamation's cursed dead are mourned, not just tallied (#155's law).
Q157.P3.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.P3.title: PORT 3 — ROOM TO MOURN THE CURSED [F2's law]

Q157.P4.body: system: [READ] / upbringing / dialogue A bait or undercover beat lets the dynast author their cover from their established character — multiple valid performances reaching the trap, not one scripted seduction. The undercover self is a choice, per KCD's lived monastery cover (#08). [PENDING, Paolo's call: the cover types.]
Q157.P4.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.P4.title: PORT 4 — AUTHOR YOUR OWN COVER [F3's law]

Q157.W1.body: Samara is a mother who will execute her child; Morinth is a child who murders for pleasure — both monstrous, both bound by a nature (law or curse) they didn't fully choose. No clean party.

Q157.W1.title: THE FORK IS TWO TERRIBLE FAMILY MEMBERS

Q157.W10.body: Players remember being ALMOST talked into siding with a serial killer — the sign the writing worked. A trap that can catch the trapper is unforgettable.
Q157.W10.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.W10.title: THE SEDUCTION OUTLASTS THE MISSION

Q157.W2.title: THE PLAYER IS THE BAIT AND THE TARGET

Q157.W3.body: The player can be talked into the wrong choice in the moment — the monster's charm works on the person meant to be baiting it, which is the rarest and best kind of test: your own judgment under pressure.

Q157.W4.body: Morinth's nature isn't her fault; her mother's law is genuinely a prison; the seduction lands because it is partly true. The killer feels, for a moment, like the victim.
Q157.W4.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.W4.title: THE MONSTER HAS A REAL CASE

Q157.W5.body: Samara's code is what lets her murder her own daughter — the quest shows the cost of absolute principle, not just its correctness.
Q157.W5.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.W5.title: THE LAW IS A TRAGEDY, NOT A VIRTUE

Q157.W6.body: The grieving mother of a real victim guides the player in, so Morinth's charm arrives already stained — the seduction fights against a corpse the player has seen.
Q157.W6.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.W6.title: THE BODY COUNT IS SHOWN FIRST

Q157.W7.body: The Ardat-Yakshi nature admits no cure; the fork admits no mercy for both. One family member dies, and the player only chooses which — the tragedy is structural.
Q157.W7.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.W7.title: NO BOTH-LIVE

Q157.W8.body: Morinth was born into a killing body; the monster is a person the nature made lethal, which is what makes killing her hard and sparing her deadly.
Q157.W8.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.W8.title: THE CURSE IS NOT CHOSEN

Q157.W9.body: Samara, if she wins, has executed her daughter and gives loyalty carrying that — the victory is a wound, not a triumph.
Q157.W9.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.W9.title: THE SURVIVOR CARRIES THE GRIEF

Q157.X1.body: Siding with Morinth is mechanically inferior (a serial killer imitating a justicar, worse for the squad, no real upside) and the game frames it as the obviously-wrong pick — so the seduction, however well-written, is a choice the player is punished for taking rather than a genuine fork. The dilemma is one-sided. LAW: if a quest offers a seductive-but-wrong choice, the choice must have a REAL upside the player forgoes by refusing it — so that resisting the seduction costs something and the temptation is genuine, not a trap with a loss attached. A seduction you're simply penalized for is a lecture; make the wrong choice genuinely tempting on the merits.
Q157.X1.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.X1.title: THE "HELP MORINTH" PATH IS A LOSING TRAP, NOT A REAL CHOICE

Q157.X2.body: The quest builds Morinth as a genuine person trapped in a lethal nature, then kills her (in the common ending) with no space to sit with what was lost — the "she is a victim too" thread is raised and dropped. The tragedy of the curse is stated but not mourned. LAW: when a quest kills a humanized monster, it must leave ROOM to mourn what the nature made unavoidable — an aftermath beat where the loss is felt, not just tallied. The fold can carry Morinth's kind forward as a grief, not a closed case (Nature of the Beast's #155 law, restated).
Q157.X2.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.X2.title: MORINTH'S PERSONHOOD DIES WITH HER, UNEXAMINED

Q157.X3.body: To bait Morinth the player must pose as her type via fixed dialogue picks; a player roleplaying differently is railroaded into the seduction script or fails the trap. The bait's performance is a corridor. LAW: a bait/undercover quest must let the player author their OWN cover from their established character, with multiple valid performances reaching the trap — not one scripted seduction. The undercover self should be a choice, not a forced role (KCD's monastery, #08, is the model for lived cover).
Q157.X3.studyTitle: THE ARDAT-YAKSHI (KILL YOUR DAUGHTER, OR BE SEDUCED BY HER) (Mass Effect 2)
Q157.X3.title: THE SEDUCTION REQUIRES A PERFORMANCE THE PLAYER CAN'T FULLY AUTHOR

Q158.N1.body: Entry: stage 2. A man who wants to be left alone, and something worse under it. > "River sent me. You okay?" [gate: none] -> the opening; his deflection, and the choice of how hard to push > (rush him / demand he snap out of it) [gate: none] TRAP -> the efficient-gamer instinct; it closes him. Every fast move is the wrong one > (slow down; ask, don't tell) [gate: none] -> the crack opens; patience is the only key NOVERB "Get you into a clinic / call someone" — the quick institutional fix is not the verb that works; Barry has to be REACHED, not processed. The removed verb is the quest's thesis: you cannot outsource this to a system; it has to be you, listening.
Q158.N1.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.N1.title: NODE H-1 — Barry at the door

Q158.N2.body: Entry: stage 3. The heart of it. Barry, if reached, talks about his dead friends and the weight. > "Tell me about them." [gate: none] -> the thread appears: the friends, the loss, the possibility of honoring them > "You couldn't have saved them." [gate: none] -> depends on tone; the wrong warmth is a dismissal, the right one is a hand > "There's a way to honor them." [gate: the thread found] -> THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK: a reason to stay, built from the grief itself, not against it > (just listen; let the silence hold) [gate: none] SILENCE -> sometimes the thing that reaches him is not a line at all; the game honors the pause WHAT THIS NODE COSTS: the player's efficiency, their comfort with grief, their instinct to fix — spent, or the man is lost.
Q158.N2.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.N2.title: NODE H-2 — the grief

Q158.N3.body: Entry: stage 4. No fanfare either way. > (reached him) [gate: patience + the thread] -> Barry lives; later, he honors his friends; the player learns it quietly, a life kept > (lost him) [gate: the wrong words] -> the player leaves; later, the absence; no "MISSION FAILED," just a man who was alive when you arrived and isn't now > NOVERB "Reload and try again" — the game offers no prompt, no ceremony; the outcome stands. The removed verb is the entire design: one try, no safety net, a life that stays lost or kept by how you spoke.
Q158.N3.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.N3.title: NODE H-3 — the outcome

Q158.P1.body: system: dialogue scenes / [READ] / the conscience system A Bohemia quest that is one conversation with one life on it — a survivor at the bottom, reachable only by patience and reading them, losable by rushing or the wrong words, with no marker for the right lines and no reload ceremony. The RESCUE-DENIAL register (our staged law) as a playable, failable intervention. ``` @TALK the_bottom speaker=barry entry=wellness_check @SAY I told River I'm fine. I'

Q158.P2.body: system: [READ] / dialogue The reaching lines are UNMARKED but LEGIBLE to attention — the grief points at the thread, listening reveals the key — so a dynast who does the emotional work reliably succeeds, and only the rushing player fails. Unmarked means "read the person," never "guess the flag." The #26/#155 fairness law, applied to compassion. [PENDING, Paolo's call.]
Q158.P2.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.P2.title: PORT 2 — UNMARKED BUT FAIR [F1's law]

Q158.P3.body: system: the fold / prior encounters The survivor on the table is someone the dynast has REASON to know — witnessed before the bottom, given texture the intervention draws on — so reaching them is knowing them, not passing a kindness check. The fold builds the person the compassion is for, across prior beats.
Q158.P3.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.P3.title: PORT 3 — THE LIFE IS A SPECIFIC PERSON [F2's law]

Q158.P4.body: system: the fold / conscience / faction memory A life lost to the dynast's failure LANDS — the grief and blame of those who loved them, the district's memory, a mark carried. The absence of ceremony is kept; the absence of consequence is not. The fold records who the dynast could not reach, and that record has weight. (Contrast Q122: no karma bar, but the world remembers.)
Q158.P4.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.P4.title: PORT 4 — THE FAILURE LANDS [F3's law]

Q158.W1.body: No combat, no puzzle, no item — a life saved or lost entirely through conversation. The genre's purest demonstration that dialogue can be the whole quest and the whole stakes.
Q158.W1.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W1.title: THE ONLY WEAPON IS WORDS

Q158.W10.body: Saved, you learn it without fanfare; lost, you learn it as an absence. The refusal to celebrate or mourn loudly is what makes it feel like a real life, not a game beat.
Q158.W10.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W10.title: THE OUTCOME IS QUIET EITHER WAY

Q158.W2.body: Barry really dies if the words go wrong — the intervention is failable without a reload prompt, which is what gives the conversation its weight. Real stakes require real failure.
Q158.W2.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W2.title: THE PLAYER CAN FAIL

Q158.W3.body: No marker, no highlight, no "correct" glow — the player must READ the man, not the UI. Compassion is a skill the player brings, not a checkbox.
Q158.W3.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W3.title: THE GAME WON'T FLAG THE RIGHT WORDS

Q158.W4.body: Efficiency, rushing, treating the NPC as a dispenser — every trained gamer reflex kills Barry. The quest is won by unlearning how you play.
Q158.W4.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W4.title: THE PLAYER'S INSTINCTS ARE THE ENEMY

Q158.W5.body: Barry is reached by honoring his dead, not by arguing him out of mourning — the solution is redirecting the pain, not denying it. Compassion that works with the wound.
Q158.W5.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W5.title: THE KEY IS IN THE GRIEF, NOT AGAINST IT

Q158.W6.body: No failure fanfare, no reload prompt — just a man who was alive and isn't. The absence of ritual is the stakes: this is what it feels like to be the one someone depended on.
Q158.W6.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W6.title: NO SAFETY NET, NO CEREMONY

Q158.W7.body: Ignore it and Barry dies off-screen; the world doesn't force you to be his rescuer. The freedom to fail by absence makes the choice to try meaningful.
Q158.W7.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W7.title: THE QUEST IS MISSABLE AND UNCHASING

Q158.W8.body: It arrives as a minor errand from River — the disguise of the small ask makes the reveal of what's actually being asked land harder.
Q158.W8.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W8.title: THE FAVOR HID THE WEIGHT

Q158.W9.body: Sometimes letting the pause hold reaches Barry better than any line — the game honors listening over speaking, the rarest dialogue-design humility.
Q158.W9.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.W9.title: SILENCE CAN BE THE ANSWER

Q158.X1.body: The lines that reach Barry are unmarked, which is the design's strength — but they are ALSO not fully legible even to a compassionate player; some correct-feeling choices fail, so a player doing genuine emotional work can still lose him to a guess. The line between "unmarked" and "unfair" is crossed here for some. LAW: an unmarked compassion quest must still be FAIR — the reaching lines must be legible to attention (the grief points at the thread; listening reveals the key), so that a player who does the emotional work reliably succeeds, and only the rushing/dismissive player fails. Unmarked must mean "read the person," not "guess the flag" (the #26/#155 earned-outcome fairness law, applied to compassion).
Q158.X1.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.X1.title: THE RIGHT PATH IS OPAQUE TO THE POINT OF LUCK

Q158.X2.body: Barry exists to be reached-or-lost; his interiority, his friends, his life before the collapse are thin, so the intervention can feel like a compassion CHECK rather than a relationship with a specific man. The stakes are real but the person is sketch. LAW: the life on the table must be a SPECIFIC person the player has reason to know — witnessed before the bottom, given a texture the intervention draws on — so that reaching them is knowing them, not passing a kindness test. The fold and prior encounters can build the person the compassion is for.
Q158.X2.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.X2.title: BARRY IS A VESSEL FOR THE MECHANIC MORE THAN A PERSON

Q158.X3.body: Barry's death, if it happens, registers as a quiet log entry; the player character does not carry it, no one holds them accountable, and the world does not change. The consequence is real for Barry and weightless for everyone else. LAW: a life lost to the player's failure must LAND on the player and the world — River's grief and blame, the district's memory, a mark the dynast carries. The absence of ceremony is right; the absence of consequence is not. The fold records who the dynast could not reach.
Q158.X3.studyTitle: HAPPY TOGETHER (YOU CAN TALK HIM DOWN, AND YOU CAN FAIL) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q158.X3.title: THE FAILURE HAS NO WEIGHT ON THE PLAYER AFTERWARD

Q159.W1.body: Not a grand evil — a father's worry for his kids and a household's small resentments, farmed by something patient. The horror is domestic, which is what makes it land.

Q159.W1.title: THE FEEDSTOCK IS ORDINARY LOVE

Q159.W10.title: THE LOGIC OUTLASTS THE QUEST

Q159.X1.body: The quest's best idea — a Prince farming a household's ordinary poisons — is mostly implied; the children's cultivation, the court's frictions, Balgruuf's love as feedstock are gestured at, not dramatized, so the domestic-harvest horror lands thinner than the concept promises. The Blade steals focus from the farm. LAW: if the horror is that ordinary emotion is FARMED, the farming must be SHOWN — the small resentments cultivated on screen, the parent's love visibly refined — so the harvest is felt, not inferred. The Amalgamation's bookkeeping on grief must be watchable, not just named (the "horror is the clipboard," Q122, restated).
Q159.X1.studyTitle: THE WHISPERING DOOR (A FATHER'S GRIEF, WEAPONIZED) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)

Q159.X2.body: Balgruuf handed the player his fear for his children and the quest never returns to him — no scene where he learns what was behind the door, no cost or relief to the parent whose love was the raw material. The human who started it is dropped. LAW: the person whose emotion was harvested must get an AFTERMATH — the parent learns, grieves, or is spared, so the harvest has a human close, not just a loot payout. The fold returns to the wounded; the harvest is not finished until its source is faced.
Q159.X2.studyTitle: THE WHISPERING DOOR (A FATHER'S GRIEF, WEAPONIZED) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q159.X2.title: THE FATHER GETS NO RESOLUTION

Q159.X3.body: Powering the Ebony Blade by killing "those who trust you" reduces, in practice, to killing generic friendly NPCs — the profound premise (trust as fuel) becomes a checklist of disposable townsfolk, draining the horror into a farming chore. LAW: if a tool runs on betrayal, the betrayed must be PEOPLE the player actually trusted — named, known, costly — so feeding it is a real severance, not a chore on strangers. Trust-as-fuel must cost trust, or it is just murder with a counter.
Q159.X3.studyTitle: THE WHISPERING DOOR (A FATHER'S GRIEF, WEAPONIZED) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q159.X3.title: THE BLADE'S BETRAYAL COST IS EASILY GAMED

The #143 verdict engine plus the #141 organ make the failure perceivable; a stake the player can't see isn't one (the #26/#154 fairness law).

Q160.P2.title: PORT 2 — THE WRONG ANSWER LANDS [F1's law]

Our regression-gate and no-brick-wall laws are the cost of shippable deduction (the #23/#45 laws).
