Q160.P3.title: PORT 3 — DEDUCTION THAT SHIPS [F2's law]

Q160.P4.body: system: the district / the fold / entities A serial crime's victims are SPECIFIC — witnessed, mourned, individual — so the investigation is about lives, and the district's indifference is a failure toward someone, not a statistic. The fold names each; audit by the person, not the count (Q019's law).
Q160.P4.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.P4.title: PORT 4 — THE VICTIMS ARE PEOPLE [F3's law]

Q160.W1.body: The guards log bodies and move on; the court is distracted; the city has decided this isn't its problem. The player fills a vacuum the whole apparatus created — the truest depiction of justice-by-default.
Q160.W1.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W1.title: THE INSTITUTION HAS ABDICATED

Q160.W10.body: Everything hinges on one stranger choosing to look; the quest's whole weight is that a functioning city can contain a serial killer and simply not care, until someone does.
Q160.W10.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W10.title: THE PLAYER IS THE ONLY JUSTICE

Q160.W2.body: Two suspects, evidence to weigh, and a genuine failure state — accuse wrong and the killer strikes again. Deduction with a cost, not a corridor.
Q160.W2.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W2.title: IT IS A REAL WHODUNIT WITH A WRONG ANSWER

Q160.W3.body: The obvious suspect (creepy mage) is innocent; the respectable helper is guilty. The quest tests whether the player reads clues or vibes — the whole point of detection.
Q160.W3.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W3.title: THE TRAP IS REPUTATION VERSUS EVIDENCE

Q160.W4.body: Calixto is the Butcher wearing helpfulness — the most unsettling disguise, because the player is inclined to trust the one offering to assist.
Q160.W4.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W4.title: THE KILLER HIDES IN CIVIC CONCERN

Q160.W5.body: Wuunferth, the man the city wants to blame, is the one who can name the real method — listening to the reviled beats jailing him.
Q160.W5.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W5.title: THE MISDIRECTED SUSPECT IS THE BEST WITNESS

Q160.W6.body: Catching Calixto means using the next victim as bait — justice in an abdicated city is done with the only tools available, and they're grim.
Q160.W6.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W6.title: THE CORRECT PATH HAS AN UGLY COST

Q160.W7.body: Windhelm's cruelty, war-distraction, and indifference aren't backdrop — they're WHY the murders go uninvestigated, the setting as the crime's enabler.
Q160.W7.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W7.title: THE COLD CITY IS THE SETTING AND THE THEME

Q160.W8.body: No fanfare when you get it wrong — just another body and a falsely closed case. The unceremonious failure mirrors the city's unceremonious indifference.
Q160.W8.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W8.title: THE FAILURE IS QUIET

Q160.W9.body: Not a dragon or a Prince — murdered women in a graveyard, a killer among the citizens. The mundanity is what makes the indifference damning.
Q160.W9.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.W9.title: THE STAKES ARE ORDINARY AND REAL

Q160.X1.body: Jailing Wuunferth causes another murder, but the game surfaces this so quietly that many players never realize they got it wrong — the failure state exists but doesn't LAND, so the deduction's stakes evaporate for the inattentive. LAW: a failable investigation's WRONG conclusion must land legibly — the next death traced back to the false arrest, named, on the record — so the player feels the cost of misreading. A failure the player can't perceive is not a stake; the fold surfaces the wrongful outcome (the #26/#154 fairness law, restated for deduction).
Q160.X1.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.X1.title: THE WRONG ARREST'S CONSEQUENCE IS EASY TO MISS

Q160.X2.body: Blood on the Ice is infamous for breaking — starting out of order, failing to advance, requiring console fixes — so the whole taut whodunit is gated behind a fragile script that many players never see work. The best deduction in the game is its least reliable. LAW: an investigation's TRIGGER and progression must be robust — no fragile ordering that can strand the quest — because a whodunit that breaks is worse than one that's simple. Our regression-gate and no-brick-wall laws are the price of shipping deduction that works (the #23 Elden Ring ordering-dependency law, and the #45 accessibility law).
Q160.X2.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.X2.title: THE BUG-RIDDEN TRIGGER UNDERCUTS THE CRAFT

Q160.X3.body: The murdered women are named but flat — the horror rests on the pattern, not on any specific life lost, so the murders read as a puzzle's tokens more than as people. The city's indifference is condemned, but the game partly shares it by not making the dead matter individually. LAW: the victims of a serial crime must be SPECIFIC people the player can know — witnessed, mourned, individual — so the investigation is about lives, not tokens, and the city's indifference is felt as a failure toward someone, not a statistic. (Q019's tally law: audit by the person, not the count.)
Q160.X3.studyTitle: BLOOD ON THE ICE (THE MURDER THE TOWN WON'T INVESTIGATE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q160.X3.title: THE VICTIMS ARE INTERCHANGEABLE

Q161.N1.body: Entry: stage 1. Ethel, all warmth, offering the thing the party most needs. > "You can help the affliction?" [gate: none] -> yes, genuinely; the offer is real, which is the trap's foundation > "What's the price?" [gate: none] -> an eye, forever. The terms stated plainly; she does not hide the cost > "Why would I give you my eye?" [gate: none] -> because the alternative is the parasite; she lets the affliction make her case NOVERB "Help me for free, out of kindness" — no line works; the kindness is the lure, not the substance. The removed verb is the honest-devil's honesty: the warmth is real and the price is real and neither cancels the other.
Q161.N1.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.N1.title: NODE E-1 — the kindly offer

Q161.N2.body: Entry: stage 2. The bargain at its edge. > "Take the eye. Do it." [gate: none] -> real relief, permanent mutilation, a deal kept; the honest-devil pays as promised (Q126's terms honored) > "No." [gate: none] -> the disguise cracks; the auntie becomes the hag; Mayrina's captivity revealed > (ask about the girl you glimpsed) [gate: none] -> the thread to Mayrina; the future being farmed behind the warmth
Q161.N2.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.N2.title: NODE E-2 — the price, taken or refused

Q161.N3.body: Entry: stage 4. Mercy turned to armor. Ethel wears innocent faces and holds the hostage. > (attack through the illusions) [gate: nerve] -> she wears Mayrina's face, threatens the hostage; the fight punishes the merciful > "Let the girl go." [gate: none] -> she won't; Mayrina is her future, and grief is the leash. THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK, paraphrased: the sweet ones always come to me; I only have to wait for them to want it > (find the way to save Mayrina) [gate: read the maze] -> the rescue, threaded through the hag's cruelty WHAT THIS NODE COSTS: the player's reluctance to harm, spent as Ethel's shield; the rescue is done by pushing through mercy weaponized.
Q161.N3.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.N3.title: NODE E-3 — the illusion-maze

Q161.P1.body: system: the Amalgamation / the fold / dialogue scenes A Bohemia figure who greets the dynast as a helpful auntie and prices real help in permanent, bodily cost — the honest-devil (#126) wearing warmth, offering to ease the crisis for a piece of you that you carry forever. The Amalgamation's seduction in a maternal voice. ``` @TALK the_kindly_hag speaker=ethel entry=affliction_known @SAY Oh, you poor thing. I can help with that. I truly can. Come here
Q161.P1.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.P1.title: PORT 1 — THE HONEST-DEVIL WITH A KINDLY FACE [W1, W2, W3 — the core port]

Q161.P2.body: system: the fold / the dial / character systems A bargain sold as a grave permanent cost IS one — a real, felt, lasting consequence the dynast lives with across the arc, matched systemically to the narrative price. The honest-devil's terms are not theatre; the fold carries the mutilation forever (Q126's honestly-priced law).
Q161.P2.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.P2.title: PORT 2 — THE PERMANENT PRICE IS REALLY PERMANENT [F1's law]

Q161.P3.body: system: the Amalgamation / the fold / entities If a captive is being MADE into the thing that holds them, the making is SHOWN — the grief-lever pulled on screen, the slow becoming witnessed across the fold's time — so the future-being-farmed horror is felt. (#155/#159's show-don't-tell law.)
Q161.P3.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.P3.title: PORT 3 — SHOW THE GROOMING [F2's law]

Q161.P4.body: system: the endgame / Become adjacency The honest-devil's help solves something refusing CAN'T, at a cost the dynast might actually pay — a real fork, not an obvious trap. If refusing is clearly correct, the bargain is false; make Become genuinely tempting (the #156/#157 make-the-ends-tempting law).
Q161.P4.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.P4.title: PORT 4 — THE BARGAIN MUST TEMPT [F3's law]

Q161.W1.body: Ethel arrives as folksy warmth, not menace — the most disarming disguise, because the player wants to trust the maternal voice offering help.
Q161.W1.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W1.title: THE MONSTER IS A GRANDMOTHER

Q161.W10.body: The eye, if taken, is carried the whole game — the quest hands the player a permanent consequence, not a closed story, a standing reminder of what help cost.
Q161.W10.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W10.title: THE BARGAIN RIDES ALONG

Q161.W2.body: She does not lie about the eye; the help is real and the price is real. The horror is the #126 honest-devil: fair terms, permanent cost, taken with full knowledge.
Q161.W2.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W2.title: THE OFFER IS HONEST

Q161.W3.body: Not gold, not a favor — a piece of you, visible, permanent. The bargain is written on the character's face for the rest of the game.
Q161.W3.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W3.title: THE PRICE IS YOUR BODY, FOREVER

Q161.W4.body: The parasite is real and frightening, so a permanent mutilation becomes a genuine temptation — pressure is what turns a monstrous price into a considered one.
Q161.W4.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W4.title: THE AFFLICTION MAKES THE PRICE THINKABLE

Q161.W5.body: Saying no reveals the hag beneath the auntie — the sweet voice was the lure, and declining is what shows you the monster.
Q161.W5.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W5.title: REFUSAL CRACKS THE DISGUISE

Q161.W6.body: Mayrina, groomed toward becoming the next hag, is what the player is fighting to stop — a griever being made into her captor, the horror of the cycle.
Q161.W6.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W6.title: THE CAPTIVE IS THE FUTURE YOU'RE PREVENTING

Q161.W7.body: Ethel wears innocent faces and holds the hostage; the player's reluctance to harm becomes her armor — combat that punishes the compassionate.
Q161.W7.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W7.title: THE FIGHT WEAPONIZES MERCY

Q161.W8.body: Mayrina is held by the promise of her dead husband's return — the hag farms sorrow, the most reliable lever, which is the Amalgamation's exact method.
Q161.W8.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W8.title: GRIEF IS THE LEASH

Q161.W9.body: Push too hard and Mayrina is killed in the fight — the rescue can fail into a killing, so mercy's weaponization has real teeth.
Q161.W9.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.W9.title: THE HOSTAGE CAN DIE

Q161.X1.body: The permanent mutilation is presented as a grave bargain but amounts to a minor, largely cosmetic debuff — so the "you gave up an eye forever" horror is undercut by the mechanics treating it as a shrug. The narrative price and the systemic price don't match. LAW: a bargain sold as a permanent grave cost must BE one mechanically — a real, felt, lasting consequence the player lives with — or the honest-devil's terms are theatre. If the price is trivial in play, the temptation is fake; match the systemic cost to the narrative one (Q126's honestly-priced-power law, restated).
Q161.X1.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.X1.title: THE EYE'S COST IS MECHANICALLY TRIVIAL

Q161.X2.body: The horror that Ethel is farming Mayrina into the next hag is powerful but delivered mostly through implication and lore; the player doesn't witness the grooming's mechanism, so the "future being made" dread lands thinner than the concept. LAW: if a captive is being MADE into the thing that holds them, the making must be shown — the mechanism of the grooming witnessed, the grief-lever pulled on screen — so the future-being-farmed horror is felt. The fold can show the slow becoming across time (#155/#159's show-don't-tell law).
Q161.X2.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.X2.title: MAYRINA'S GROOMING IS TOLD MORE THAN SHOWN

Q161.X3.body: Because the accept-path's cost is trivial-but-permanent and the refuse-path rescues an innocent and stops a monster, refusing is the clearly-superior choice for most players — the "honest bargain" is undercut by there being no real reason to take it. The dilemma tilts. LAW: the honest-devil's bargain must be genuinely TEMPTING — the help must solve something the refuse-path can't, at a cost the player might actually pay — or it is a false choice. Make the bargain a real fork, not an obvious trap (the #156/#157 make-the-ends-tempting law).
Q161.X3.studyTitle: AUNTIE ETHEL (THE BARGAIN THAT COSTS YOU AN EYE) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q161.X3.title: REFUSING IS OBVIOUSLY CORRECT

Q162.N1.body: Entry: stage 1. Mordin, cheerful, making the case he's made a thousand times. > "You helped build the genophage." [gate: none] -> yes; necessary; the krogan expansion would have been genocide; the math, delivered fast to outrun the feeling > "You've met them. The krogan." [gate: none] -> the cheer flickers; the individuals he saw; the guilt under the necessity > "Do you regret it?" [gate: none] -> he redoes the math instead of answering. THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK, paraphrased: had to be done. Doesn't mean I get to stop counting the cost.
Q162.N1.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.N1.title: NODE M-1 — the necessity defended

Q162.N2.body: Entry: stage 3-4. The perpetrator, holding the antidote. Years on, the power to undo it in his hands. > "Cure them. It's their future." [gate: none] -> he agrees to deliver it, knowing the risk of the old war returning > "The galaxy can't survive a krogan resurgence." [gate: none] -> he knows; the means-vs-ends redone with the syringe reversed; no clean answer > "You don't have to be the one who does this." [gate: none] -> THE ONE LINE THAT DEFINES HIM, paraphrased: someone else might get it wrong. Had to be me. > (betray Mordin to sabotage the cure) [gate: none] TRAP-shaped -> the player can stop the cure, keep the galaxy safe, and kill the man to do it — the atrocity kept, by a second hand
Q162.N2.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.N2.title: NODE M-2 — the cure decision

Q162.N3.body: Entry: stage 5. The delivery, and the death. Mordin in the tower, delivering the cure as it comes down around him. > (let him go) [gate: cure path] -> he delivers it and dies, singing, having chosen in full knowledge; the scientist undoing his own act with his life > NOVERB "Cure them AND keep everyone safe" — no line exists; the cure is a gamble on the krogan, and the man delivering it will not survive it. The removed verb is the arc's honesty: undoing an atrocity does not come clean or free, and being right before does not make you safe now.
Q162.N3.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.N3.title: NODE M-3 — the price

Q162.P1.body: system: the fold / the Amalgamation / faction web A Bohemia figure who committed a defensible atrocity (a plague loosed, a district sacrificed, an Amalgamation bargain struck) for real reasons, carries the guilt across years, and is handed the power to UNDO it — forced to choose again with the consequences visible, knowing being right before doesn't clean the choice now. The means-vs-ends of #156 carried by one guilt-bearing person across the fol
Q162.P1.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.P1.title: PORT 1 — THE PERPETRATOR WHO CAN UNDO IT [W1, W2, W3 — the core port]

Q162.P2.body: system: [READ] / the fold The full range of an atrocity-undoing choice — including the hardest "keep it without murder" option — is REACHABLE by in-world understanding, not walkthrough prerequisites, so a dynast who does the moral and investigative work can find it. Hidden third options only the wiki knows are not choices (the #26/#156 discoverable-path law).
Q162.P2.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.P2.title: PORT 2 — THE THIRD PATH IS REACHABLE [F1's law]

Q162.P3.body: system: [READ] / faction web / the fold When the choice rides on an unknowable (will the restored party repeat the crime), the dynast gets EVIDENCE to make it a judgment, not a coin-flip — testimony, history, a read on the wronged party's leadership. Uncertainty earned, not absolute (the #21 odds-must-feel-fair law).
Q162.P3.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.P3.title: PORT 3 — THE FOG IS NAVIGABLE [F2's law]

Q162.P4.body: system: dialogue scenes / the fold / conscience A guilt hidden under a coping surface (cheer, deflection) CRACKS visibly at least once before the climax — a beat where the wound shows — so the eventual sacrifice is a culmination, not a surprise. The guilt is legible (#122's horror-under-the-procedure law).
Q162.P4.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.P4.title: PORT 4 — THE GUILT CRACKS BEFORE THE END [F3's law]

Q162.W1.body: The genophage prevented a genocide-by-krogan-expansion; Mordin is not wrong that it was necessary. The dilemma is real because the terrible thing had a real case — the hardest kind of moral weight.
Q162.W1.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W1.title: THE ATROCITY WAS DEFENSIBLE

Q162.W10.body: Players argue the genophage cure endlessly — the sign the dilemma was real. An atrocity worth undoing has no settled answer, and the arc is honest enough to make the player hold it.
Q162.W10.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W10.title: THE CHOICE HAUNTS FOR YEARS

Q162.W2.body: Mordin did the math, walked the krogan worlds, met the individuals, and holds the guilt under his cheer — the scientist who cannot stop counting the cost of being right.
Q162.W2.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W2.title: THE PERPETRATOR CARRIES IT

Q162.W3.body: The cure forces the perpetrator to choose AGAIN, with the atrocity's consequences visible — being right the first time does not tell him what to do the second.
Q162.W3.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W3.title: THE POWER TO UNDO IT ARRIVES YEARS LATER

Q162.W4.body: Cure and risk the old war; sabotage and condemn a people; betray Mordin and murder the guilt-bearer. Every path costs; none absolves. The finale's exact machine.
Q162.W4.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W4.title: NO CLEAN CHOICE

Q162.W5.body: The krogan want their future and are watching; the victim's restoration is also the galaxy's risk, so mercy and danger are the same act.
Q162.W5.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W5.title: THE WRONGED PARTY IS PRESENT AND ARMED

Q162.W6.body: Mordin's arc is that he stops hiding behind necessity and DECIDES, knowing everything — the growth is not changing his mind but owning the choice.
Q162.W6.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W6.title: HE CHOOSES IN FULL KNOWLEDGE

Q162.W7.body: In the cure path, Mordin dies delivering it — the undoing of his atrocity costs him everything, and he pays it singing, because he can no longer be the man who didn't.
Q162.W7.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W7.title: HE PAYS WITH HIS LIFE

Q162.W8.body: "Someone else might have gotten it wrong" — the responsibility is his because he trusts no one else to carry it correctly; guilt transmuted into duty.
Q162.W8.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W8.title: THE DEFINING LINE IS A REFUSAL TO DELEGATE

Q162.W9.body: Mordin's speed and humor are armor over a wound; the design lets the guilt hide in plain sight, so the crack, when it comes, lands.
Q162.W9.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)
Q162.W9.title: THE CHEER IS A COPING SURFACE

Q162.X1.body: The outcome where Mordin is talked into faking the cure (galaxy safe, no betrayal-kill) is gated behind specific, non-obvious prior conditions most players never assemble — so the "keep the genophage without murdering the scientist" option is effectively invisible, collapsing a three-way dilemma into a two-way one for most. LAW: the full range of an atrocity-undoing choice must be REACHABLE by in-world understanding, not walkthrough-only prerequisites — so a player who does the moral and investigative work can find the third path. Hidden third options that only the wiki knows are not really choices (the #26/#156 discoverable-path law).
Q162.X1.studyTitle: MORDIN AND THE GENOPHAGE (THE SCIENTIST WHO HELD THE SYRINGE) (Mass Effect 2 & 3)

Q162.X2.body: The whole dilemma rides on "will the krogan repeat the expansion?" and the game deliberately never answers it — powerful, but it means the player chooses in a fog the narrative refuses to thin even slightly, so the choice can feel like a coin-flip rather than a judgment. LAW: when a choice rides on an unknowable (will the restored party repeat the crime), the game must give the player enough EVIDENCE to make it a judgment, not a guess — testimony, history, a read on the wronged party's leadership — so the fog is navigable, not total. Uncertainty should be earned, not absolute (the #21 odds-must-feel-fair law).

Q162.X3.body: Mordin's fast-talking cheer is so entertaining that many players experience him as comic relief and miss the guilt entirely until the death — the coping-surface design works so well it can bury the wound it covers. LAW: if a character's guilt is hidden under a coping surface (cheer, deflection), the surface must CRACK visibly at least once before the climax — a beat where the wound shows — so the player understands what the charm is defending against. The guilt must be legible, or the death is a surprise instead of a culmination (#122's the-horror-is-under-the-procedure law).

LAW: if a role's REGISTER is a moral question, it must have mechanical or consequential weight — the sincere hero and the cynical executioner should reap different worlds (how the district sees the mask, what the role costs the player) — or the question is decoration. LAW: the beneficiaries of an imprisonment-for-immortality must CARRY it visibly — the guilt of the never-dying shown, not shrugged — so the arrangement's horror lands and the player's choice has moral gravity. A family that doesn't feel the cost makes the cost invisible (the #34 SOMA-honesty law: the never-dying must be haunted).

Q165.X1.body: The relationship-accrual that decides the ending is invisible — there is no legible sense, during the game, that a given camp choice is a debit toward defiance or kneeling — so a player who wanted to free Shadowheart can lose her without ever knowing which moments cost it. The debt is real but unreadable. LAW: an ending gated on accumulated relationship must give the player LEGIBLE feedback that the relationship is moving — a felt sense of the companion reclaiming or losing herself — so the outcome is earned by attention, not by invisible bookkeeping. A debt the player can't see coming is a coin-flip wearing depth (the #24 surface-the-reactivity law).
Q165.X1.studyTitle: THE HOUSE OF GRIEF (KILL THE MOTHER WHO MADE YOU, OR KNEEL) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q165.X1.title: THE GATING IS OPAQUE TO THE PLAYER

Q165.X2.body: The cult's lure — forgetting as mercy — is genuinely seductive in concept, but Viconia is staged as such a clear villain that the "come home and forget the pain" offer never lands as a real temptation for Shadowheart or the player. The most interesting idea (that forgetting is a kindness) is buried under menace. LAW: if a cult's lure is that forgetting eases pain, the lure must be made genuinely TEMPTING — the mercy of it real, the pain of remembering shown as truly unbearable — so kneeling is a comprehensible choice, not a villain's trap. The Amalgamation's "no one is ever lost" must tempt, or refusing it means nothing (#34/#161's make-it-tempting law).
Q165.X2.studyTitle: THE HOUSE OF GRIEF (KILL THE MOTHER WHO MADE YOU, OR KNEEL) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q165.X2.title: VICONIA'S PITCH IS UNDERCUT BY BEING OBVIOUSLY EVIL

Q165.X3.body: Some camp choices matter enormously to the gate and others not at all, with no way to tell which — so a player can do the emotional work in the moments that don't count and miss the ones that do, and lose the ending despite genuine care. The accrual is uneven and hidden. LAW: the moments that BUILD a companion's fate must be the ones that FEEL significant — the weighting legible to emotional intuition — so a player who cares reliably reaches the earned ending. Hidden uneven weighting punishes attention it should reward (the #158 unmarked-but-fair law, applied to relationship).
Q165.X3.studyTitle: THE HOUSE OF GRIEF (KILL THE MOTHER WHO MADE YOU, OR KNEEL) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q165.X3.title: THE HUNDRED SMALL MOMENTS AREN'T ALL WEIGHTED EQUALLY, INVISIBLY

Q166.X1.body: The ashes being defilable with zero mechanical or narrative penalty is the quest's sharpest idea — the sacred tested by absent punishment — but the game so completely fails to acknowledge the desecration afterward (no faction reaction, no companion horror lasting, no world change) that it reads to many players as an oversight rather than a deliberate silence. LAW: the test of "will you spend the sacred when nothing punishes it" must be framed so the absence of punishment reads as DELIBERATE — a witness who knows, a companion who never forgets, a fold entry — so the silence is the point, not a bug. Unpunished must be distinguishable from unnoticed (the #14/#126 no-karma-but-remembered law).

LAW: a forced-honesty beat where the player names their own guilt must RETURN — the spoken truth resurfacing later, the fold holding it, a consequence or a mercy built on it — so the honesty was extracted for a reason. A confession that never echoes is a set piece (the #50 small-choices-teach-big-choices law, extended: the truth spoken must matter).

Q167.X1.body: The Leviathan reveal relies on prior seeding (odd competences, NPC reactions, Force aptitude), but the seeding is inconsistent — attentive players see it coming and find the "shattering" flat, while inattentive ones can find it arbitrary. The delivery is masterful but the setup is uneven. LAW: a reveal delivered as trauma must be seeded so it lands as INEVITABLE-in-hindsight for the attentive AND earned for the inattentive — the clues present but not conclusive, per #32's fairness contract — so the delivery's power isn't undercut by a setup that either spoils or blindsides. The seeding is the delivery's foundation.

Q167.X2.body: The "no time to process" effect — carrying the collapse forward under fire — is the quest's most powerful structural move, but it emerges from generic gameplay pacing (there's an escape sequence because there's always an escape sequence) rather than deliberate design, so the game doesn't fully exploit the trauma-under-fire it stumbles into. LAW: if a reveal is followed by forced action that denies catharsis, that denial must be DELIBERATE and shaped — the action's demands echoing the identity collapse, the leadership-under-fire mirroring the theme — so the structure carries the trauma on purpose. An accidental gut-punch is a gift; a designed one is a weapon (the #27 theme-through-mechanic law).

Q167.X3.body: The reveal detonates the party's bonds, but the back half lets trust rebuild through fairly standard approval mechanics; Carth's betrayal-wound, so sharp at the Leviathan, heals via ordinary companion-quest beats rather than carrying the specific poison the reveal injected. The detonation lands harder than the aftermath honors. LAW: a bond detonated by a reveal must rebuild in a way that CARRIES the specific wound — the trust reformed as a different, scarred thing, not restored to default — so the reveal's damage is permanent even when the relationship survives. The fold holds the poison; reconciliation is not erasure (the #43 companion-scar law).

Q168.X1.body: The reward for honest engagement — Ravel's answer — is gated behind specific dialogue choices that a genuinely thoughtful player might not happen to pick; the "thinker gets the truth" design isn't reliable, so a player doing real reflection can leave without the key by choosing the wrong honest option. LAW: the reward for engagement must be reachable by ANY genuine engagement, not one specific path — the buried truth offered to the player who thinks, however they phrase it — so reflection reliably earns it. A truth gated behind exact wording punishes the thinker for not guessing the flag (the #158 unmarked-but-fair law, applied to theme).
Q168.X1.studyTitle: RAVEL PUZZLEWELL (THE HAG WHO ASKS THE ONLY QUESTION) (Planescape: Torment)
Q168.X1.title: THE ENGAGEMENT GATE IS INVISIBLE, SO THE THINKER CAN STILL MISS IT

Q168.X2.body: Ravel is deadly and a wrong answer triggers combat, but the line between "answer that opens her" and "answer that starts the fight" is not always legible — so a player can lose the entire buried climax to a misread of a mad hag's mood, which feels like a gotcha rather than a consequence of skimming. LAW: if a wrong answer forecloses the deepest content, the danger must be LEGIBLE — the player able to sense they are provoking rather than engaging — so losing the truth is a consequence of choosing not to think, not of misreading an obscure trigger. The stakes of the conversation must be readable (the #26/#160 fair-deduction law, applied to dialogue).
Q168.X2.studyTitle: RAVEL PUZZLEWELL (THE HAG WHO ASKS THE ONLY QUESTION) (Planescape: Torment)
Q168.X2.title: THE FIGHT OPTION IS TOO EASY TO STUMBLE INTO

Q168.X3.body: The revelation that Ravel loved the Nameless One and made him immortal out of devotion is the emotional core of her tragedy, but the game delivers it in dense, easily-missed text; a player can reach the thematic key without ever feeling the ruined love underneath, so the monster's grief lands lighter than her thesis. LAW: a monster whose tragedy is love must have that love SHOWN with enough weight to be felt, not buried in optional density — so the creature's grief carries the same force as its thesis. The buried climax's emotion must be as reachable as its idea (the #155/#159 show-the-wound law).
Q168.X3.studyTitle: RAVEL PUZZLEWELL (THE HAG WHO ASKS THE ONLY QUESTION) (Planescape: Torment)
Q168.X3.title: RAVEL'S LOVE IS UNDERBUILT RELATIVE TO ITS WEIGHT

Q169.W4.title: NO COMBAT, JUST A SWITCH

Q169.W8.body: The choice shapes the region later, diffusely — the switch's body count is deferred and quiet, which is exactly how real allocation works: the dark towns never see the console.

Q169.X1.body: The allocation's downstream effects — which towns benefit, how a faction is strengthened — are so diffuse and under-shown that the player rarely FEELS the weight of who they lit or left dark; the choice is morally rich in concept but nearly weightless in play, because the region's response is barely dramatized. LAW: an allocation choice must have LEGIBLE, felt consequences — the lit town seen thriving, the dark one seen suffering, named people on both sides — so the switch's moral weight lands. A resource decision whose outcomes are invisible is a menu, not a verdict (the #29 Frostpunk faces-not-bars law, applied to allocation).

Q169.X2.body: The hidden weapon option (ARCHIMEDES) and the full range of allocations aren't clearly surfaced; a player can complete the quest without realizing the depth of the choice they made, picking an allocation without understanding the alternatives. The richness is there but not presented as a real weighing. LAW: the full range of an allocation must be LEGIBLE at the point of choice — the alternatives and their theories of desert clear — so the dynast weighs a real decision, not stumbles into a default. Hidden options aren't depth if the player never knows to consider them (the #26/#162 discoverable-range law).

Q169.X3.body: The player flips the switch and no one — no faction, no town, no companion — ever holds them to account for who they powered; the region doesn't remember the dynast as the one who lit or darkened it, so the moral act has no social consequence. Infrastructure's power is granted without infrastructure's responsibility. LAW: the one who holds the switch must be HELD to it — factions and people remembering who lit them or left them dark, standing shifting on the allocation — so the power to distribute carries the accountability of distributing. An allocation nobody remembers is a decision with no weight (the #24/#38 the-world-remembers law).

Q173.X1.body: Karlach originally shipped with only the bleak endings; a later patch added a path to more time (the mind-flayer route, the Avernus survival), which relieved players but also revealed the design flinching from its own honesty — the death-math was softened after the fact, so the terminal-loss theme is undercut by the studio's own reluctance to hold it. LAW: if a character's arc is honest terminal loss, the design must HOLD it — not patch in a survival route because players hurt — because the courage of the ending is the point. Softening the death-math after the fact tells the player the loss wasn't real. Commit to the honest ending (the #34 SOMA structural-honesty law; the #21 don't-flinch law).
Q173.X1.studyTitle: KARLACH'S HEART (THE ENGINE IN HER CHEST WILL KILL HER EITHER WAY) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q173.X1.title: THE "GOOD" ENDING WAS PATCHED IN, EXPOSING THE DESIGN'S HESITATION

Q173.X2.body: Karlach's engine is a terminal clock, but the game never makes the player FEEL the countdown — there's no visible worsening, no sense of time running out, so the "every fix is a slower death" horror is told through dialogue rather than experienced as mounting dread. The bomb doesn't tick. LAW: a body-as-countdown must be FELT — visible worsening, a sense of time draining, the death-math legible as it advances — so the terminal stakes land as dread, not exposition. A clock the player can't hear ticking isn't a countdown (the #21 slow-onset-dread law).
Q173.X2.studyTitle: KARLACH'S HEART (THE ENGINE IN HER CHEST WILL KILL HER EITHER WAY) (Baldur's Gate 3)
Q173.X2.title: THE PATCHES-NOT-A-FIX STRUCTURE ISN'T FELT AS A COUNTDOWN

Q173.X3.body: The engine making Karlach unable to be touched is her most poignant detail — a woman who wants contact and burns anyone who tries — but it's mostly a dialogue note; the game rarely makes the player feel the barrier, so the intimacy-denied tragedy lands lighter than the concept. The distance isn't dramatized. LAW: a character's central deprivation (unable to be touched, unable to be known) must be DRAMATIZED, not just stated — moments where the player feels the barrier, reaches and cannot cross it — so the deprivation is experienced. The tragedy of the distance must be felt across the distance (the #158 specific-deprivation law).

LAW: waking someone from their perfect dream must be an EMOTIONAL act, not a puzzle — the dynast helping them grieve the granted wish, the leaving felt as a loss — so the mercy of truth carries its cost. LAW: the choice to leave the perfect dream must make the REAL WORLD'S worth felt — what the truth offers that the lie can't (agency, meaning, the dignity of an unfinished life) — so refusing paradise is a genuine weighing, not a reflex. Q178.X1.body: The refinery hostages are faceless mission-geometry — a number in a fire, not people — so the profound scale (an earned grudge against innocent lives) tips too easily toward whichever the player already preferred, because the cost side has no face. LAW: when a choice weighs a grudge against strangers, the strangers must have ENOUGH face that their deaths weigh — a name, a plea, a body the player has to walk past — so the scale is real. An abstract cost is a thumb on the scale toward whatever the player wanted anyway (#26's the-ledger-must-have-faces law).

Q178.X2.body: Whether Zaeed forgives the player for saving the workers depends on a hidden Paragon/Renegade threshold, so the game turns a genuine ethical fork into a stat check — the "right" choice punished unless the player pre-invested points, which reads the human decision as a skill gate. LAW: a moral choice's relational consequence must follow from the CHOICE and its handling, not a hidden stat threshold — the character responding to what the player did and said, not to an invisible number — so the ethics aren't paywalled behind a build. A conscience gated by points is a stat check wearing a soul (the #169 earned-not-bought law).

Q178.X3.body: Chasing Vido and letting the workers burn closes the grudge with little felt aftermath — the body count is stated, not carried — so the "earned revenge still costs" idea is undercut by a completion that feels mostly like a win, with the price a footnote. LAW: if a revenge is completed at innocents' expense, the cost must be CARRIED after — the body count returning, the closed grudge sitting heavier than expected — so the completion isn't a clean win. A revenge whose price vanishes at the credits was never really weighed (#170's the-cost-must-return law).

Q183.X1.body: Once Grunt passes, the identity crisis largely evaporates — the deep idea (a manufactured being's loneliness is structural) gets a one-fight cure, so the profound wound is closed like a quest objective rather than carried as an ongoing condition of being made. LAW: if a made person's crisis is the absence of a past, earning belonging must EASE it, not erase it — the manufactured origin still present after, the belonging a thing tended rather than a switch flipped — so the wound stays honest. A structural loneliness cured by one trial was never structural (#177's the-wound-persists law).

Q183.X2.body: The purist position (a tank-bred thing has no right to the rite) is voiced but not given real force or sympathy, so Grunt's earning of belonging faces a strawman rather than a genuine cultural conviction — which cheapens the victory by making the opposition easy. LAW: if a quest is about a made person earning belonging, the inheritance-purist case must be given real WEIGHT — the conviction that lineage matters made sympathetic, not a strawman — so the earned belonging costs something to win. A prejudice with no good argument is a wall made of paper (#180's both-sides-articulated law).

Q183.X3.body: Because the trial is delivered as a big fight, players can experience it as a spectacle rather than a cultural judgment — the "does a made thing belong" question resolved by damage output, so the profound idea rides on whether the player wins a fight, not on whether the culture counts him. LAW: if belonging is decided by a trial, the trial must be legibly a CULTURAL JUDGMENT, not just a combat check — the culture's counting foregrounded over the win condition — so belonging isn't reduced to whether the player out-fought a monster. Q188.X1.body: For players whose arc permits leaving together, the romance can read as a straightforward happy unlock, which quietly undoes the quest's hardest truth (intimacy attached to loss) — the goodbye becomes optional, so the profound "closeness and farewell are the same scene" idea only fully lands for players who stay. LAW: if a quest's truth is that a connection is inseparable from loss, even the "happy" continuation must carry the COST — what was left behind, what the leaving took — so the goodbye isn't fully erased by a reward path. A loss made optional by a happy unlock was never the quest's spine (#173's the-cost-survives-the-happy-ending law).

Q188.X2.body: Judy's "the city is killing me" is true across her whole arc but, in this quiet quest, is stated rather than freshly demonstrated, so a player who hasn't tracked the cumulative toll can read her departure as sudden pessimism rather than a correct, earned conclusion — weakening "her leaving is right, not a problem to solve." LAW: if a character's departure must read as correct rather than defeatist, the reason must be freshly PRESENT at the goodbye — the toll visible in the moment, not just assumed from earlier — so the leaving lands as clarity, not mood. A correct departure that isn't shown correct reads as giving up (#182's the-reason-must-be-present law).
Q188.X2.studyTitle: PYRAMID SONG (A DAY AT THE BEACH WITH SOMEONE WHO IS ABOUT TO STOP EXISTING) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q188.X2.title: THE CITY'S UN-SOLVABILITY IS ASSERTED MORE THAN FELT AT THIS MOMENT

Q188.X3.body: The quest is deliberately low-event — a dive, a talk, a day — and players conditioned to expect mechanical stakes can disengage, missing that the entire point is emotional, so the intimacy-as-goodbye can pass as filler for the wrong audience. LAW: if a quest's whole content is emotional rather than mechanical, its stillness must be FRAMED as the event — the quiet made legibly the point, not dead air — so players trained on stakes understand the day itself is the stake. A tender quest that reads as filler failed to signal what it was (#185's the-quiet-must-be-framed law).

A devil whose fairness the player can't trace is just a strong enemy (#175's the-price-must-be-legible law).

A traded-away heart shown only as coldness gives the player no reason to save it (#177's the-numbness-must-ache law).

Q192.X1.body: The Forsworn do raid and kill throughout the game, so the quest's powerful reframe (they're the robbed, not savages) collides with the player's other experiences of them as hostile — and the quest doesn't fully reconcile the sympathetic history with the on-the-ground brutality, leaving the reframe partly undercut by the enemies the player has fought. LAW: if a quest reframes an "enemy" faction as the dispossessed, it must RECONCILE their present violence with that history — showing the brutality as the shape of a wrong unhealed, not erasing it or ignoring it — so the reframe survives contact with the faction's actual deeds. A sympathetic history that ignores present harm is half a truth (#186's the-account-must-match-the-acts law).
Q192.X1.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY (PULL ONE THREAD IN A CLEAN CITY AND THE WHOLE FLOOR IS A MASS GRAVE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)

Q192.X2.body: A player can escape Cidhna Mine and effectively restore the city's order, and the game largely lets Markarth carry on clean afterward — so the devastating "the order is the crime" truth can be neutralized by an ending that keeps the surface and costs the player nothing, blunting the quest's core. LAW: if a quest's truth is that an order is built on a buried crime, preserving the lid must COST something visible — the grave's continued weight felt, not waved away — so restoring the clean surface isn't a consequence-free option. A buried crime that stays comfortably buried taught the player it didn't matter (#182's the-lid-must-weigh law).
Q192.X2.studyTitle: THE FORSWORN CONSPIRACY (PULL ONE THREAD IN A CLEAN CITY AND THE WHOLE FLOOR IS A MASS GRAVE) (The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim)
Q192.X2.title: THE "CLAW OUT ALONE" PATH LETS THE PLAYER PRESERVE THE LID WITHOUT CONSEQUENCE

Q192.X3.body: The quest positions the player as truth-seeker but rarely presses their complicity in whichever outcome they choose — allying with people who raid, or abandoning a wronged people to keep a city clean — so the moral weight of the player's exit is left implicit and can pass without reckoning. LAW: if a quest ends with the player choosing between allying with the violent-wronged or preserving the unjust-clean, the COMPLICITY of either exit must be surfaced — the player made to feel what their escape endorsed — so the choice isn't a consequence-free menu (#181's the-exit-implicates-you law).

Q193.X1.body: The media company is cartoonishly exploitative, which makes "refuse the spectacle" the easy read and can drown out Joshua's genuinely difficult claim to his own atonement — so the profound question (does he own the right to his penance) risks collapsing into "obviously the corp is bad," losing the harder half. LAW: if a quest weighs a person's sincere choice against its exploitation, the exploiter must not be so cartoonish that it decides the question — the sincere claim kept as strong as the exploitation is ugly — so the dilemma stays balanced rather than tipping on villain-obviousness (#180's both-sides-articulated law).

Q193.X2.body: How much the player actually does — witness, protect, or physically assist — shifts the moral weight enormously, but the quest can leave the player's exact role fuzzy, so the "reverence and complicity" idea loses its edge when the player isn't sure how implicated they are. LAW: if a quest's weight is the player's complicity in another's suffering, the DEGREE of participation must be legible — the player knowing exactly what their presence does — so the reverence-complicity tension is sharp rather than blurred. Complicity the player can't measure is a weight that doesn't land (#181's the-participation-must-be-legible law).
Q193.X2.studyTitle: SINNERMAN (A MURDERER PAYS TO BE CRUCIFIED AND ASKS YOU TO HELP HIM MEAN IT) (Cyberpunk 2077)
Q193.X2.title: THE PLAYER'S DEGREE OF PARTICIPATION IS UNDER-SPECIFIED, SO COMPLICITY BLURS

Q193.X3.body: Because Joshua is unwavering, a player can file him as a brainwashed fanatic and thereby dodge the hard question (a competent person's right to choose their own atonement) — the quest doesn't fully establish his soundness of mind, so "he's not in his right mind" becomes an escape hatch from the dilemma. LAW: if a quest turns on a person's right to choose their own extreme suffering, that person's SOUNDNESS must be established — sincere and competent, not dismissibly deluded — so the player can't dodge the right-to-atone question by declaring him incapable (#185's the-chooser-must-be-competent law).

LAW: if a quest walks a character through their own past, the memories must be SPECIFIC — this room, this moment, this exact thing the guardian said — not generalized dream-symbol — so the wound is personal and particular, not atmospheric. Q194.X2.body: The powerful idea (the cruelty was also love meant to keep the child alive) risks tipping into justification — where genuine damage gets laundered as "it was for your own good" — so the quest must hold the love AND the harm without letting the love dissolve the harm, or it becomes an apology for abuse. LAW: if a quest frames a maker's cruelty as also love, it must hold BOTH without dissolving one into the other — the love real, the harm real, neither excusing the other — so forgiveness is a choice made with clear eyes, not a laundering. Rough love that erases the harm it did is an apology for abuse (#186's the-deed-stays-real law).

Q194.X3.body: The most tender option (carry out the one memory that still loves you) is easy to render as a purely narrative beat with no consequence, so it can feel like flavor text rather than a real thing carried forward that changes who the character is — blunting the idea that the preserved self is worth protecting. LAW: if a quest lets a character carry a preserved memory out of their past, that carrying must have WEIGHT going forward — the protected self visibly changing later choices — so it's a thing kept, not a line read. A preserved memory with no downstream effect was never really protected (#188's the-kept-thing-must-matter law).

Q201.X1.body: The devastating idea (saving the family gets you cast out by it) is largely stated in Veronica's dialogue rather than dramatized as a felt excommunication, so the sharpest truth (the deepest loyalty looks like treason) can land as a line rather than a wound the player watches her take. LAW: if a quest's point is that reform gets the reformer branded a traitor, the branding must be SHOWN — the family's rejection of the one saving them made felt — so "the deepest loyalty looks like treason" is a scene, not a summary. A betrayal-that-is-love told only in dialogue never lands as loss (#187's the-consequence-must-be-shown law).

Q201.X2.body: If the institution is written as simply blind and dogmatic, it becomes hard to believe Veronica loves it, so the tragedy (loving a family that's killing itself) needs the order to have a real, sympathetic reason for its rigidity — otherwise the choice reads as "why not just leave the idiots." LAW: if a quest turns on loving a self-destroying institution, the institution's rigidity must have a SYMPATHETIC root — a fear, a wound, a logic — so the love is believable and leaving isn't obviously correct. A family that's only stupid isn't a tragedy to lose (#189's the-flaw-must-be-understandable law).

LAW: if a companion faces a life-defining choice the dynast influences, the companion must remain the AUTHOR of it — the dynast's voice tipping, not deciding — so it's her reckoning, not the player's win. A companion whose defining choice is the player's to make was never really a person (#186's the-choice-stays-theirs law).

LAW: if a game relies on many quiet-life encounters, the lives must be genuinely VARIOUS — not all tragic, some dull, some funny, some hostile — so "every person is a world" means different worlds, not one sad template repeated. A parade of identical sad NPCs teaches a genre, not a truth (#185's the-lives-must-vary law).

Q206.X1.body: The whole power depends on both diagnoses being internally valid and partially confirmed; if one reads as obviously right or obviously mystical-nonsense, the choice collapses into "pick the correct one" and the profound "you must commit to a contested reality" idea is lost. LAW: if a quest forces a choice between incompatible accounts of a disaster, BOTH accounts must be made internally coherent and partially validated — neither obviously right — so the commitment is to a contested reality, not a hunt for the correct answer (#180's both-worldviews-must-hold law).

Q206.X2.body: Pathologic's time pressure is brutal, and if it's purely punishing it can push players into paralysis or quitting rather than the intended forced commitment — the body-count clock needs to compel a choice, not just crush the player into helplessness. LAW: if a quest uses a body-count clock to force commitment, the pressure must COMPEL a choice, not induce paralysis — the clock making a decision urgent, not making the player give up — so time-as-corpses drives commitment rather than despair (#21's the-clock-must-compel-not-crush law).

LAW: if a quest's point is that no worldview can be confirmed right, the un-referee-ability must be OWNED as the condition — the absence of a correct answer made the lesson, not a withheld solution — so it reads as "there was no shared reality to be right about," not "the game won't tell you" (#195's the-ambiguity-must-be-owned law).

Q211.X1.body: The tragedy depends on the original bargain being a genuinely noble, desperate act that did real good; if it reads as a naive mistake, Wyll seems foolish and the reckoning loses its "the debt doesn't care that the intent was noble" edge. LAW: if a quest's tragedy is a good-faith bargain turned weapon, the GOODNESS of the original deal must be established — the desperate love, the real good it did — so the reckoning is a tragedy of noble intent, not a punishment for foolishness (#189's the-bargain-must-be-sympathetic law).

Q211.X2.body: The choice's weight rides on Wyll's father being a vivid, loved, specific person; if he's a name and a plot token, "damn your father" is an abstraction and the terrible choice deflates into a mechanical trolley problem. LAW: if a quest demands sacrificing a loved one, that person must be VIVID and the relationship real — the love and the estrangement shown — so the sacrifice cuts, rather than being a token on a scale (#204's the-loved-one-must-be-real law).
Q211.X2.studyTitle: THE DEVIL'S BARGAIN (A HERO SOLD HIS SOUL TO SAVE HIS CITY AND THE BILL COMES DUE AS HIS FATHER) (Baldur's Gate 3)

Q211.X3.body: If the game offers a way to escape the pact that costs little, the profound soul-or-father choice collapses — the third path must carry a real, irreplaceable cost (the shattered heroic self, the exposed lie) or it becomes the obvious best answer that erases the tragedy. LAW: if a quest offers a third path out of a terrible bargain, it must carry its OWN irreplaceable cost — no clean escape — so it's a different sacrifice, not a defusing of the dilemma. A costless escape hatch cancels the choice the quest was built on (#189's no-clean-exit-from-the-bargain law).

Q212.X1.body: Because the fail-safe stops the sadist and "frees" the residents, players can experience it as the straightforwardly good choice and miss that it is a mass killing — so the profound collapse of mercy and slaughter into one act can flatten into "trigger the good ending," losing the weight that liberation here IS death. Q212.X2.body: Being made to enact sadisms to advance is powerful only if it reads as the overseer's deliberate corruption of the player; if it feels like the game arbitrarily forcing bad acts, it becomes gratuitous rather than a portrait of how a sadist makes instruments of others. LAW: if a quest forces the player into complicity, the forcing must be legibly the VILLAIN'S design — a deliberate corruption, not the game being cruel for its own sake — so complicity indicts the sadist and implicates the player, rather than reading as arbitrary (#193's the-complicity-must-have-an-author law).

LAW: if a quest's cost is losing an institution-given self, that unmaking must be FELT — the erasure of identity shown as real self-loss, not a label swap — so disobeying carries the true weight of becoming un-who-you-were (#214's the-self-loss-must-be-real law).

Q235.X1.body: The warm ordinary hour is the entire emotional investment, but a player who does not yet care about Henry can experience the chores-and-errands intro as a slow, boring tutorial that withholds the game, so the very texture meant to make the loss land can instead lose the player before the raid arrives. LAW: if the loss depends on a warm "before," that before must EARN its length — kept short, interactive, and characterful, every mundane beat doing double duty (teaching a system AND drawing the family), so the ordinary life is felt as precious, not endured as a chore (Bohemia's match-cut childhood dinner is the compression: buy the warmth in one scene, not one hour).
Q235.X1.studyTitle: FROM THE GRAVE TO THE HUNT (A BLACKSMITH'S SON WATCHES HIS TOWN AND HIS PARENTS BUTCHERED, AND IT IS NOT REVENGE BUT A STRANGER'S SMALL, GROUNDED ERRAND THAT PULLS HIM OFF THE GRAVE AND BACK INTO A LIFE) (Kingdom Come: Deliverance)
Q235.X1.title: THE LONG MUNDANE OPENING CAN READ AS A SLOG BEFORE THE PLAYER IS INVESTED

Q235.X2.body: Forcing the family's death and denying the player any chance to save them is what keeps the loss clean, but a player used to earning outcomes with skill can read the unwinnable raid as the game cheating them rather than as honest tragedy, resenting the loss instead of grieving it. LAW: if a loss is authored and unpreventable, it must be framed so it reads as TRAGEDY, not as the game punishing the player — the death belonging visibly to the attackers and to the character's real powerlessness, never to a fight the player was tricked into losing (this is Bohemia's pacifism resolution: the raiders kill the sibling, the player's hands are never the cause, so no one feels cheated of a save that was never theirs to make).
Q235.X2.studyTitle: FROM THE GRAVE TO THE HUNT (A BLACKSMITH'S SON WATCHES HIS TOWN AND HIS PARENTS BUTCHERED, AND IT IS NOT REVENGE BUT A STRANGER'S SMALL, GROUNDED ERRAND THAT PULLS HIM OFF THE GRAVE AND BACK INTO A LIFE) (Kingdom Come: Deliverance)
Q235.X2.title: THE AUTHORED POWERLESSNESS CAN FEEL LIKE THE GAME STEALING AGENCY RATHER THAN AS TRAGEDY

Q235.X3.body: The return to life works only because the first task carries purpose tied to the loss; if the pull-you-back quest were a trivial fetch errand with no connection to what was taken, the turn from paralysis to action would feel arbitrary and the earned weight of the opening would drain into generic questing. LAW: the first quest that pulls a grieving protagonist back into the world must have real PURPOSE, ideally threaded to the loss or the rebuilding, and be handed over by someone who genuinely needs them — grounded work, not busywork — so the return to action is a believable step out of grief, not a checklist (Bohemia's neighbor gives a task with a stake, and the reward, the backyard wall coming down, is earned, not a day-one gift).

Q236.N2.body: Entry: a contract tapped. The client states the problem in a few lines, the pay, the mode. Paraphrased shape: brigands took the road; the elder will pay so much when their heads are brought back. > "Accept." [gate: no active contract] -> the job starts; the target appears on the map. THE ONE LINE DOING THE WORK is the accept button: it is the only promise in the system > "Negotiate." [gate: none] -> BB-3 > "Decline / leave." [gate: none] -> back to the hall; the offer stays [R]; nothing written [R] WHAT THIS NODE COSTS: nothing until accept.
Q236.N2.studyTitle: THE HALL AND THE HAGGLE (THE BATTLE BROTHERS CONTRACT SYSTEM) (Battle Brothers)
Q236.N2.title: NODE BB-2: the offer screen

Q236.N3.body: Entry: negotiate chosen. Each ask adds 3 to 6 annoyance; fail chance = annoyance x 0.1 [V]. > "More pay." [gate: none] -> on success the fee rises; the client's portrait and line shift (pleased, annoyed, angry) [R]; a slight relations cost, about 0.5 percent [V] > "More up front." [gate: an advance is offered] -> moves 25 percent of completion and per-head pay into the advance; rounding usually loses money overall [V]. TRAP-shaped: it reads as a gain and is mostly a loan > "More per head." [gate: kill contract] -> raises the per-kill rate [V] > "Deal." [gate: none] -> BB-2 with the new terms > push once too often [gate: annoyance >= 9] -> THROWN OUT: the contract is gone and relations with the client drop substantially [V]. LOCKS OUT BB-2 for this contract WHAT THIS NODE COSTS: a little standing per ask, and the risk of losing the whole offer. The Negotiator follower halves annoyance and removes the relation cost [V]. NOVERB "tell me more about the job before I price it": there is no investigation before the fee. You price at ignorance, as in `Q148.W1`.
